natural_language: Show all orders and the corresponding customer email addresses.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.email FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Find all products in the 'Electronics' category that cost less than 100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics' AND cost < 100;

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold by each employee in the central region, but only include employees whose total sales across products exceed 20 items.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: List each customer's email and the number of products they purchased, only for customers who have purchased more than 5 products.
sql_query: SELECT c.email, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.email HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 5

natural_language: Find the top 5 customers by total spent who have made more than 5 orders, along with their respective cities.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.city, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.city HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5 ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Retrieve a list of products that have been ordered by VIP customers, including the total quantity ordered and their average price.
sql_query:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.segment = 'vip'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name;

natural_language: Find products in the fashion category with price less than $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'fashion' AND price < 30;

natural_language: Calculate the average price of products sold by each customer segment, considering only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(p.price) AS avg_product_price FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment HAVING AVG(p.price) < 150

natural_language: Retrieve the customer full names and the total number of their orders grouped by each customer, including those who haven't completed any orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: List all products sold by customers in the retail segment with total sales exceeding $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Get the total amount of orders for each employee in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'central' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get customer segments that have an average order total greater than $400 while also identifying the total order count for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 400

natural_language: Identify the product categories that have a total revenue greater than the average revenue across all categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.category FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > (SELECT AVG(total_revenue) FROM (SELECT SUM(oi2.quantity * oi2.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi2 JOIN orders o2 ON oi2.order_id = o2.order_id GROUP BY oi2.product_id) AS subquery);

natural_language: List the order details of employees who have a commission rate higher than the average commission rate of all employees.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, o.total_amount, e.full_name FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.commission_rate > (SELECT AVG(commission_rate) FROM employees);

natural_language: List customers along with their respective order counts for cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in each order.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id;

natural_language: Retrieve products that are named 'Gadget X'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name = 'Gadget X';

natural_language: Show the average price of products sold in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(order_items.unit_price) AS average_price FROM order_items JOIN orders ON order_items.order_id = orders.order_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the count of all products in the Fashion category.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) as product_count FROM products WHERE category = 'Fashion';

natural_language: Find distinct customer segments and their order counts.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Calculate the total number of orders and total revenue for each product and list them in order of revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

natural_language: Retrieve all order items for a specific product with ID 9.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE product_id = 9;

natural_language: Select customers who are not from Seattle.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city != 'Seattle';

natural_language: List customers and the count of their pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS pending_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Determine the most sold product in each region, including only products that have been sold in at least 4 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.region, p.product_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 4 ORDER BY e.region, total_sold DESC

natural_language: List customers who live in 'Los Angeles' or 'San Francisco'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city IN ('Los Angeles', 'San Francisco');

natural_language: Determine the most popular product among corporate customers based on the total number of orders and the total sales generated.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_orders DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve the order IDs and their statuses for orders placed by 'corporate' customers in 'Miami'.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND c.city = 'Miami';

natural_language: Retrieve the count of completed orders and the corresponding total revenue for products in the 'electronics' category, grouped by product name.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS completed_orders_count, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List the unique categories of products that have generated sales for customers in the corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT p.category FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Find all products that are in the 'Clothing' category and cost more than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Clothing' AND cost > 50;

natural_language: Get the total quantity of products sold for each category where total sales exceeded $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id INNER JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 500

natural_language: Find the number of distinct products sold and the total sales amount for each customer in the retail segment, but only include customers who have ordered more than 2 different products.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_products, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 2

natural_language: Find the average total amount of completed orders by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_total_amount FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List all orders that were created in the year 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2022;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders along with the employee's full name who handled the order.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in completed orders for each segment of customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(p.price) AS average_product_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the total revenue from each product category, but only include categories that have generated more than $10000 in total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000

natural_language: Retrieve the full names of customers along with the total amounts of their orders that are cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_cancelled FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total sales by product for orders that have been cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get all order items with a quantity less than 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE quantity < 5;

natural_language: Get the names of customers who have placed orders without going back to their previous orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status IN ('completed', 'pending');

natural_language: Find all orders with a total amount between $100 and $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount BETWEEN 100 AND 200;

natural_language: Get the names of customers who have ordered products from the 'electronics' category and whose total spending exceeds $1000.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000;

natural_language: Identify the top 5 products by revenue generated from completed orders and their respective categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Identify the average price of products sold to corporate customers, including only those corporate customers who have made at least one purchase.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_product_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 0

natural_language: Identify the customers who have spent more than the average across all orders and the details of their last order.
sql_query: WITH avg_spending AS (SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS avg_total FROM orders) SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, o.order_id, o.total_amount, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.total_amount > (SELECT avg_total FROM avg_spending) ORDER BY o.order_date DESC;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales amount of products from each category, filtering to only include categories where total sales are below 20000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) < 20000

natural_language: Get all orders from the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 day';

natural_language: Select all products in the 'furniture' category with a price greater than 200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture' AND price > 200;

natural_language: Get the total cost of products in the 'Furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(cost) FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture';

natural_language: Get the top 5 employees with the highest total sales and the number of orders they processed, including their average order values.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Get the top 5 products by total quantity sold for each employee, including the employee's name and commission rate.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.commission_rate, p.product_name ORDER BY e.full_name, total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Find the total number of different products sold and the average order amount for orders placed by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS different_products, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Determine the most recent order date for each customer along with their full name and the status of their latest order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date, o.status FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, o.status HAVING NOT MAX(o.order_date) IS NULL

natural_language: Retrieve the total revenue for each product category in completed orders, but exclude categories with revenue less than 2000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) >= 2000

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders and the customers who made them.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the names of employees and the status of the orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, orders.status FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers whose email contains 'gmail.com'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%gmail.com%';

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of customers in each city along with their respective segments, showing only cities with more than 5 customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.segment, COUNT(c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers AS c GROUP BY c.city, c.segment HAVING COUNT(c.customer_id) > 5

natural_language: Find the total commission earned by employees based on their sales.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) as total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the best-selling product and the total revenue it generated, considering only orders from VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Summarize the total revenues from each product category, only for categories that have more than $10,000 in total sales, including the count of how many products fall under each category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS total_products FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000

natural_language: Get all products that cost more than $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > 100;

natural_language: Find the customers who have ordered more than the average total spent across all customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM (SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) AS avg_totals)

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and the average selling price for each category where total products sold exceeds 100.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Get the total number of orders with a 'completed' status.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

natural_language: Identify the customers who frequently buy products from the same category, where the average spending does not fall below a certain threshold.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, p.category HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 200

natural_language: List the products that have been sold more than 100 times in total along with their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Find products that are priced between $10 and $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 10 AND 20;

natural_language: Retrieve the order details and corresponding product prices for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, oi.unit_price, oi.quantity FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find all orders with a total amount less than or equal to $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount <= 50;

natural_language: Show the names of customers and the status of their latest order.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.status FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.order_date = (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders WHERE customer_id = customers.customer_id);

natural_language: Calculate the total cost of products sold in completed orders for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: Find the total sales amount and average order amount for each customer segment, listing only those segments with total sales over $10,000.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: List the email addresses of corporate customers who have completed their orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List employees along with the average total amount of completed orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the top 3 customers by total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Retrieve all customer records without specifying a segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment IS NOT NULL;

natural_language: Find all employees from the east region who have processed completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'east' AND orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the total amount of sales generated by products that have a price greater than $50, for each customer segment, but only including completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.price > 50 AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find all retail customers and their respective order totals.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS order_total FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Get the count of orders placed by each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Identify employees who have a higher average order value than the average for all employees.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS employee_average FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders)

natural_language: Find the average order amount for corporate customers for completed orders, grouped by employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: List all customers who have ordered products from at least two different categories, along with their total spending and the number of distinct categories ordered.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS distinct_categories FROM customers AS c INNER JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id INNER JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) >= 2

natural_language: Retrieve products that are priced between $20 and $75.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 20 AND 75;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders placed after March 1, 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2021-03-01';

natural_language: List the products that have been ordered by VIP customers, showing the total quantity sold and the total revenue for each product. Only include products with total revenue greater than $5,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 5000

natural_language: Find the average number of items per order for each employee, but only include employees who have processed more than 15 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_items_per_order FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 15

natural_language: Retrieve all orders with a status of 'completed' and total amount below $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount < 100;

natural_language: Select all products that have a price lower than the cost.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < cost;

natural_language: Determine the average number of items per order for each customer segment and the segment with the highest average.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(item_count) AS avg_items_per_order FROM (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS item_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id) subquery JOIN customers c ON subquery.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY avg_items_per_order DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List the customers from the VIP segment who have made purchases from more than 3 different product categories.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS unique_categories FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Find the total number of orders and the average order value for corporate customers by region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Find customers who have a higher total spending than the average spending of all customers, displaying their full names and total amounts.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM (SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) AS avg_spending)

natural_language: List all products with a price greater than $50 but less than $150.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > 50 AND price < 150;

natural_language: Get all corporate customers who signed up after January 1, 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND signup_date > '2020-01-01';

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total sales amount and the total quantity sold, including the category of each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find all completed orders with a total amount greater than $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount > 100;

natural_language: Show all employees who have a full name containing 'John'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name LIKE '%John%';

natural_language: Show the average number of products per order for each employee, considering only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(num_products) AS average_products_per_order FROM (SELECT o.order_id, o.employee_id, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS num_products FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id) AS order_summary JOIN employees e ON order_summary.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders from the last year.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 year';

natural_language: Identify products that have been ordered at least 10 times and calculate the total revenue generated from each.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS times_ordered, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) >= 10

natural_language: Find all customers from a specific city along with their order status.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Get all orders made by customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip');

natural_language: Retrieve all orders that are cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Calculate the percentage of completed orders relative to total orders for each employee, filtered by region, and show the results with employee names.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, (SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(o.order_id)) AS completion_percentage FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name, e.region

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of unique customers and total sales for products in the 'Furniture' category sold through completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS unique_customers, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE p.category = 'Furniture' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the average total spending for customers who have placed more than 5 orders and the total number of unique products they ordered.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spending, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_ordered FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Get a report of the average order total by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in the 'retail' segment by the number of orders placed by customers from 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND c.city = 'New York'

natural_language: Retrieve the list of each product along with its average price and total quantity sold in orders associated with customers in the corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, AVG(p.price) AS avg_price, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name;

natural_language: Determine the products that have never been sold and the categories they belong to.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category FROM products p WHERE p.product_id NOT IN (SELECT oi.product_id FROM order_items oi)

natural_language: Get the highest total order amount for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(o.total_amount) AS max_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Select all order items where the unit price is less than 10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price < 10;

natural_language: List all orders with a total amount between $200 and $1000.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount BETWEEN 200 AND 1000;

natural_language: Get all canceled orders along with the customer emails.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.email FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: List all products that have the name starting with 'A'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE 'A%';

natural_language: Retrieve the product with the highest selling price and the customer's details who purchased it.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.price, c.full_name, c.city FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE p.price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM products);

natural_language: Find the number of orders and the average total amount for each product category, filtered by customers in the corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the total number of order items and total sales for all orders made by customers from the city 'New York', only including those where total sales exceed $15,000.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_items, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.city = 'New York' GROUP BY c.city HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 15000

natural_language: Get the names of products that were ordered by customers in the city 'New York', along with their total sales amount, but only include products sold from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve order IDs and their statuses for orders placed by customers from the city 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Find all order items associated with a specific product ID.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE product_id = 1;

natural_language: Calculate the average commission rate of employees who have sold products in the 'Electronics' category, considering only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(e.commission_rate) AS avg_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Show all employees who are in the west region and have a commission rate less than 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'west' AND commission_rate < 0.05;

natural_language: Find all pending orders that belong to customer ID 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND customer_id = 5;

natural_language: Get all customers who have an email containing 'gmail'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%gmail%';

natural_language: For each product, calculate the total quantity sold and the total revenue, but only include products that have been sold in 'pending' orders and categorize them by segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM products p INNER JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY p.product_name, c.segment;

natural_language: Find the most popular products in terms of quantity sold among corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC;

natural_language: List all order items for a specific order.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 7;

natural_language: Show the customers who have placed orders with a total amount greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: List the employees and the number of retail customers they have served, including only those customers who made at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS retail_customers FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all unique product categories.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products;

natural_language: Get all the orders' total amounts along with the corresponding customer segments.
sql_query: SELECT o.total_amount, c.segment FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

natural_language: Get orders with a total amount less than $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount < 200;

natural_language: Get all customers who live in 'Austin' or 'Dallas'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city IN ('Austin', 'Dallas');

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount spent by VIP customers on their orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Calculate the average order amount and total orders for products in a specific category, filtering out categories with fewer than 10 total orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 10

natural_language: Get the total number of customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers;

natural_language: List all products in the category 'electronics' that have been ordered more than 10 times in completed orders, including their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Display the names of employees and the total commission they earned from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount * employees.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: List all orders with a total amount equal to $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount = 50;

natural_language: Find all orders where the total amount is less than $10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount < 10;

natural_language: Find the number of unique products bought by each customer segment and the total sales amount for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS unique_products_bought, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Get all orders from customers with the full name 'John Doe'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE full_name = 'John Doe');

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 customers who have spent the most money, along with their segment information.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.segment ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Determine the total number of different products sold and their total revenue per category, but only include categories that sold over 50 products.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) > 50

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders along with the full names of the customers who made them.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_id, orders.order_date FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get all orders with a total amount greater than $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 200;

natural_language: Show the total number of completed orders per customer along with their names.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_completed_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Show all products that belong to the 'Furniture' category with a price below $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture' AND price < 200;

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have a cost greater than $20 but less than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > 20 AND cost < 50;

natural_language: Find the total revenue generated from 'books' category products, including only orders that have a status of 'completed' and total amounts greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'books' AND o.status = 'completed' AND o.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Find the employees and their commission rates for orders that have been marked as pending.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Select all orders placed in the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 day';

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who live in Chicago.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chicago';

natural_language: Find the average quantity ordered per order for products in the 'Electronics' category, but only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity_per_order FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Identify the customers who have ordered more than 5 different products and spent over $800 in total.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 5 AND SUM(o.total_amount) > 800

natural_language: Retrieve a list of customers who have made more than two orders and the average amount spent per order by each of them.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 2

natural_language: Identify the products that generated the highest revenue from corporate customers, grouped by product name.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

natural_language: Calculate the total quantity of products ordered by corporate customers in the west region for orders that were completed.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND c.city = 'west' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Show the total amount of orders and corresponding employee names.
sql_query: SELECT orders.total_amount, employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id;

natural_language: Identify the most valuable customer in terms of total spend, along with the total number of orders placed.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve the average order total for corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: List the top 3 products by total sales amount, only considering completed orders in the 'corporate' segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get the list of customers with the highest total spending, including their segment, sorted in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.segment ORDER BY total_spent DESC

natural_language: Get the revenue generated by products in each category, showing only categories with revenue above $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Identify the product categories where the total quantity sold exceeds 200, and show the corresponding total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 200

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and total sales amount for each employee, restricting to those employees who made more than $5,000 in sales.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: List all products with their respective order counts, including those products which have been sold more than 10 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: Get the sum of total amounts from all completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total_completed_amount FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

natural_language: Show employees who have worked on orders with a total amount greater than 1000.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders made in the past week.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 day';

natural_language: Show all employees in the 'east' region with a commission rate less than or equal to 15%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'east' AND commission_rate <= 0.15;

natural_language: Get a summary of order status counts for orders made by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: Get the names and emails of customers who placed orders between January 1, 2023, and March 31, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.order_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-03-31';

natural_language: Show the count of different products purchased by each customer, focusing on those who've made at least 3 purchases.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS product_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3

natural_language: Find all employees located in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM employees WHERE region = 'central';

natural_language: Show the product names and their total sales for products sold by employees in the 'west' region during the current year, filtering out products with sales under 1,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Get a list of unique cities from which customers have placed orders, excluding duplicates.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales from orders for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Get the customer names and their first orders, including the order date and total amount, filtering for customers who have only made one order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_date, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) = 1);

natural_language: List the customers who have only ordered products in the 'Clothing' category and their total spending, but only include those who spent more than $1,000.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Clothing' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Find the top 5 products by total sales amount for each region.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, e.region, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY p.product_name, e.region ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Find the total quantity of items ordered for each product in completed orders, filtering for products with total quantities greater than 20.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: List the top 5 most expensive products.
sql_query: SELECT product_name FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List all products sold with their total sales amount, but only for products that have been sold more than 20 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Get orders placed after June 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2023-06-01';

natural_language: List all completed orders along with the customers' full names and their cities.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name, c.city FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find all orders with a total amount less than 500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount < 500;

natural_language: Retrieve all products with a cost greater than $10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > 10;

natural_language: Find all products along with their prices that have been ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

natural_language: Find customers who signed up in 2023 and their order statuses.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.signup_date >= '2023-01-01';

natural_language: List all products along with their total sales amount and cost.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales, p.cost FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, p.cost;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders from employees in the 'central' region.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM employees WHERE region = 'central');

natural_language: Identify products that have been ordered in more than 15 different orders, along with total quantity sold, and only include products that sold more than 100 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 15 AND SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have a cost greater than their price.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > price;

natural_language: List all customers who have made orders along with the total amount of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Identify the customers who have placed orders totaling more than 5000 but have only made one order.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 1 AND SUM(o.total_amount) > 5000

natural_language: Identify the products that have been ordered more than 50 times across all orders, showing their names and total quantities ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Display the full name of each VIP customer along with their signup date.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.signup_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get the count of cancelled orders for each city, along with the total number of orders from each city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city

natural_language: List customer details for customers who made orders in the last month and spent more than the average order amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.email, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month' AND o.total_amount > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders);

natural_language: Get the number of customers in each segment who have never placed a completed order, including the segment and the customer count.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 0

natural_language: Find the average order amount for each customer segment and the number of customers in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Determine the customer who has spent the most money in total along with the number of orders they placed.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Show the list of cancelled orders along with the customer email.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.email FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Find the total commission earned by employees from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount * employees.commission_rate / 100) AS total_commission FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.employee_id;

natural_language: Get a list of employees who have not handled any cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' IS NULL;

natural_language: Find the number of products sold and the total revenue per category for orders handled by employees from the western region.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find all order items with a unit price of 20 or more.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price >= 20;

natural_language: Find all corporate customers who signed up in 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND signup_date >= '2022-01-01' AND signup_date < '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Get the number of distinct customers who have made orders in each city, only for cities with more than 3 distinct customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) > 3

natural_language: Show the names of employees who have at least one completed order.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find all products that cost less than $5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost < 5;

natural_language: Determine the total sales by category for products sold by employees from the west region, showing only categories with total sales greater than 10000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000

natural_language: List all products that have never been ordered, along with the total number of orders and average order amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 0;

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold by each employee in their respective regions, including only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, AVG(p.price) AS avg_product_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Find the average commission rate of employees who processed orders for VIP customers with a total amount exceeding $200.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(e.commission_rate) AS avg_commission_rate FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.total_amount > 200;

natural_language: Show all orders from customers in the 'corporate' segment.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.full_name FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Find the total number of orders and the average order value for each customer segment, including both completed and pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the email addresses of customers who live in 'New York' and have placed any orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of completed orders grouped by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Show the emails of all customers who signed up in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT email FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= '2023-01-01';

natural_language: List employees and how many orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS processed_orders FROM employees LEFT JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Find the top 10 products by total orders and calculate the percentage of total sales they represent.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_orders, (COUNT(oi.order_item_id) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM order_items) * 100) AS sales_percentage FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_orders DESC LIMIT 10;

natural_language: List all customers who signed up in March 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2022-03-01' AND '2022-03-31';

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have never been sold (not in order_items).
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_items);

natural_language: Get the list of customers and the total number of orders for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS completed_order_count FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Find the total amount of completed orders along with the corresponding customer names.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) as total_sales, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Identify products that have been sold in more than 15 different orders and their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) > 15

natural_language: Find the employee with the highest total commission from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name ORDER BY total_commission DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Count the number of customers in 'corporate' segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Show the orders with their statuses and the corresponding employee names.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, orders.status, employees.full_name AS employee_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id;

natural_language: List the total sales amount grouped by each customer's segment.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: List all customers who have placed more than 5 orders, including their total spent and segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Get the count of unique products sold and the total sales amount for completed orders per customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_sold, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the names of products and the total quantity sold for each, grouped by category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category, p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the total quantity sold and average price of products in the 'Electronics' category, including only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Determine the total quantity of products sold in each category, only for products that generated more than $20,000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 20000

natural_language: List the customers who have made at least 3 orders, showing their names and the total amount spent, ordered by the total amount in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3 ORDER BY total_spent DESC

natural_language: List all orders made by customers in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail');

natural_language: Get the total order amounts for completed orders by each customer.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Determine the number of orders for each status (completed, cancelled, pending) for different customer segments, showing the count per segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment, o.status

natural_language: Calculate the total number of products sold per category in completed orders, filtering for categories with more than 100 products sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: List the total revenue generated by each product category, excluding those categories with total revenue under 5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: List all customers in 'Chicago' who are 'corporate'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chicago' AND segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get the average price of all products sold in orders completed by 'vip' customers, only including products that have been sold at least 5 times.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) >= 5

natural_language: Find all employees in the central region with a commission rate of 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'central' AND commission_rate = 0.05;

natural_language: Retrieve a list of customers whose total number of orders exceeds the average number of orders across all customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) AS avg_count);

natural_language: Find all customers in the 'vip' segment who have made purchases over $500.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip' AND orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Find the average commission rate for employees who have processed cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(employees.commission_rate) AS average_commission FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: List product categories along with the average cost of products in each category, and also the total number of products in that category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.cost) AS average_cost, COUNT(p.product_id) AS total_products FROM products p GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List the cities along with the count of customers from each city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who live in 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Get the total quantity of products sold for each product category in the last month, filtering out any category with less than 50 total units sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 MONTH' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) >= 50

natural_language: List customers who have purchased products from more than 2 different categories and their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 2

natural_language: List the employees who have a commission rate greater than the average commission rate across all employees, along with their total sales.
