sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.commission_rate HAVING e.commission_rate > (SELECT AVG(commission_rate) FROM employees)

natural_language: Identify the customers who have ordered more than 3 different products, including their segment and total different products ordered.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS total_different_products FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 3

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who have made at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders);

natural_language: Get the average order total for each employee by region, including the number of orders they have processed, filtering out those with less than 5 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region, e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 5

natural_language: Retrieve the yearly sales for each customer segment, displaying the segment and total sales for each year.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) AS year, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment, year ORDER BY year;

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold and the total revenue generated from those products for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Find the products that have generated more than 1000 in total sales along with their categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: List all products sold in completed orders along with the total quantity sold for each product, only for those sold by employees from the west region.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Calculate the total sales for each category of products sold in completed orders, and include only categories with sales greater than $15,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 15000

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total revenue generated from completed orders for corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get the total spent by each customer for products in the 'electronics' category, but only include customers who have a corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who signed up in the last week.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 day';

natural_language: Get the names of customers who have pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 products by total sales amount, including their category, but only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find the total earnings by city for employees who sold more than $2,000 worth of products.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) AS total_earnings FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) > 2000

natural_language: Find the highest-selling product along with its total revenue and the number of unique customers who purchased it.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get the number of unique customer segments.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT segment) FROM customers;

natural_language: Identify customers who have ordered products from at least 3 different categories and calculate their total spending. Display customer ID, name, number of categories, and total spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) >= 3

natural_language: Find the total sales amount for products in the 'Electronics' category sold by employees in the west region, filtering to only include totals greater than $2000.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND e.region = 'west' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: Retrieve the product categories that have not seen any purchases in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT p.category FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date < NOW() - INTERVAL '1 month' OR o.order_id IS NULL GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find employees who have not processed any orders in the last month and the total revenue they would have earned, calculated from their average commission rate and the average order value.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, (AVG(o.total_amount) * e.commission_rate) AS potential_revenue FROM employees AS e LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 MONTH' GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 0

natural_language: Calculate the total number of products ordered and total income generated by each employee for completed orders, only showing those with total income over $15000.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(oi.product_id) AS total_products_ordered, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_income FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 15000

natural_language: Find all customers in the corporate segment who signed up in 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2021;

natural_language: Retrieve a list of customers who have never placed an order, along with the total number of orders in the database.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL; SELECT COUNT(order_id) FROM orders;

natural_language: List the total quantity of each product ordered, but only for products that have been ordered in more than 5 different orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Find all orders that were placed after April 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2023-04-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the count of orders per customer segment and their average order total.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Show the names of customers who have made purchases and their respective signup dates.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Analyze the total sales and average quantity sold for each product, filtering out products that do not achieve at least $2,000 in sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: Get all pending orders that were made in February 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND order_date >= '2023-02-01' AND order_date < '2023-03-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the average order total grouped by employee and city for completed orders, but only include averages above $300.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, c.city, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name, c.city HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 300

natural_language: Get the names of customers who have placed orders along with their cities.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.city FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id;

natural_language: Get the email addresses of customers along with the total amounts of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.email, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the total price for products sold in completed orders, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) as total_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Display the total number of orders and the average order amount for each customer segment, segmented further by the status of the orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment, o.status;

natural_language: Get the total amount of completed orders and the respective customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount), c.segment FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List the customer segments along with the number of orders for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS number_of_orders FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 products by total sales amount for the last quarter.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 month' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get the average price of products sold in completed orders by customer segment, including the segment name in the result.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(p.price) AS average_product_price FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the top 5 products by total sales revenue, where each sale is linked to a completed order.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Show the total revenue generated from each product in the last month, but only include products with total revenue greater than $200.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 MONTH' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 200

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales by region for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Retrieve the average price of products sold by each employee in the east region, filtering for quantities greater than 10.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE e.region = 'east' AND oi.quantity > 10 GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the number of products sold and total revenue generated from completed orders for each product category, including only those categories that generated more than $10,000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS products_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 10000

natural_language: Find the customers from the east region whose total order amount exceeds the average order amount of all completed orders.
sql_query: WITH avg_order AS (SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS avg_amount FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed') SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city IN (SELECT DISTINCT city FROM employees AS e WHERE e.region = 'east') GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT avg_amount FROM avg_order)

natural_language: Identify the three most profitable products based on total revenue generated, along with their category.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3

natural_language: Get the segments of customers who have ordered products only from the 'home' category and the number of customers in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'home' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get a report of products categorized as 'electronics' that have been sold more than 20 times, showing the total quantity sold and total sales revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales for each product, along with the number of unique customers who purchased that product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name

natural_language: Get the total sales amount by product for cancelled orders but only include products with total sales greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 500

natural_language: List all orders with their items for cancelled statuses.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, order_items.product_id, order_items.quantity FROM orders JOIN order_items ON orders.order_id = order_items.order_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Get all products with the name 'Chair'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name = 'Chair';

natural_language: Get a summary of total costs by product category, only for products sold in completed orders where the total cost exceeded $800.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM order_items AS oi INNER JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id INNER JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) > 800

natural_language: Determine the most popular product in terms of units sold and its total revenue, considering only products sold in orders marked as completed.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List all employees with a commission rate higher than 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate > 0.05;

natural_language: Retrieve customers with the email domain 'gmail.com'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%@gmail.com';

natural_language: List all products that were sold in orders that had a total amount greater than $1000, along with the number of times they were sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS times_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.total_amount > 1000 GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: Identify all products that were sold more than 100 times in total and their total revenue, including the respective categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Get all products with the name containing 'chair'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%chair%';

natural_language: Display the order dates and total amounts for orders placed by customers in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_date, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.city IN (SELECT city FROM employees WHERE region = 'east');

natural_language: Identify the customers who have made purchases from more than three different product categories in the last year.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 YEAR' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Retrieve total order amounts for all orders made by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Show the total number of products sold and the total revenue generated from 'vip' customers who made orders in the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 day';

natural_language: List all customers who live in Los Angeles and are in the corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Los Angeles' AND segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: List all customers from the 'corporate' segment and their order totals.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS order_total FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Get the number of products sold and total revenue for each category that has generated over 5000 in sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Determine the product categories that generate the highest total revenue, along with their total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 10000

natural_language: Get all employees from the east region with a commission rate of 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'east' AND commission_rate = 0.05;

natural_language: Find all customers who live in the city of Seattle.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Seattle';

natural_language: Get a summary of orders showing the customer full name and the order total for each order.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the segment of customers who have purchased products from the 'Electronics' category and have an order total over $500, displaying the count of such customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) as customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.total_amount > 500 GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of orders made by each VIP customer in the city of New York, along with the names of the employees who handled those orders, and the total number of items ordered, grouped by customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name AS customer_name, e.full_name AS employee_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_items_ordered FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND c.city = 'New York' GROUP BY c.customer_id, e.employee_id;

natural_language: List all products with a total order quantity of over 100, segmented by category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated by orders from the 'Sports' category that were completed, grouped by month.
sql_query: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) AS order_month, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Sports' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date)

natural_language: Find the count of distinct customers who made purchases on or after January 1, 2022, for each product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2022-01-01' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in the 'electronics' category, along with the total quantity sold and only include those where the total quantity sold exceeds 100.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS average_price, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Find employees who have sold products averaging more than $100 and the total sales they generated.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING AVG(oi.unit_price) > 100

natural_language: List all customers who have signed up in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Get all employees with a commission rate less than or equal to 0.1.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate <= 0.1;

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered more than ten times by customers who are 'retail' segment, displaying product name and total quantity ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_ordered FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Retrieve all order items related to product ID 3.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE product_id = 3;

natural_language: List all employees who have a commission rate of exactly 15%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate = 15;

natural_language: Get a summary of orders, showing the total number of completed and cancelled orders for each customer, listed by customer name.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id

natural_language: Fetch the total amount spent per customer for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated from orders for products in each category sold to corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Retrieve all active customers who signed up after January 1, 2022, along with their cities.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.signup_date > '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Find the total number of products in the 'clothing' category.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = 'clothing';

natural_language: List customers from the VIP segment who have made orders greater than the average order total for all customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.total_amount > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders);

natural_language: List of completed orders with their total amounts filtered by a specific employee's name.
sql_query: SELECT o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.full_name = 'John Doe' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated by each segment from orders placed in the last two years, comparing it to the previous two years.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '2 year' THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END) AS current_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_date < CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '2 year' THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END) AS previous_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Show the names of employees who processed any pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Determine the total sales for each employee, categorized by their region and segment of customers they served.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.region, c.segment ORDER BY total_sales DESC;

natural_language: Show all orders along with the employee who processed them.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, employees.full_name AS employee_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id;

natural_language: Get the list of products that have never been ordered, including their price and cost, along with the total number of units sold for those products that have been ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price, p.cost FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL UNION SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price, p.cost FROM products p INNER JOIN (SELECT oi.product_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY oi.product_id) AS sold ON p.product_id = sold.product_id;

natural_language: Find the total number of orders placed by a specific customer ID.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 1;

natural_language: Get the average price of products sold in completed orders, segmented by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the most popular product in terms of quantity sold from orders placed by corporate customers, including the total revenue from that product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve the top 3 products with the highest profit margin, calculated as (price - cost) and display their names and margins.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, (p.price - p.cost) AS profit_margin FROM products p ORDER BY profit_margin DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get a list of employees with a commission rate of 0.1 or higher.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate >= 0.1;

natural_language: Get the total sales amount for each product category, including the number of orders and the average order total, grouped by region and segmented by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, e.region, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category, e.region, c.segment ORDER BY e.region, p.category;

natural_language: Find all products and the total quantity sold, ordered by quantity sold in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_sold FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name ORDER BY total_sold DESC;

natural_language: List all orders placed in the month of January.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 1;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and the total revenue generated for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and total sales amount for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the list of all completed orders along with the customer's city.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.city FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List all products that have been sold more than 10 times in completed orders, along with the total quantity sold and total revenue generated.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Calculate the total sales and profit margin for each product category sold to retail customers only.
sql_query:
SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity * (oi.unit_price - p.cost)) AS total_profit 
FROM order_items oi 
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id 
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id 
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id 
WHERE c.segment = 'retail' 
GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the average price of all products.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(price) AS average_product_price FROM products;

natural_language: List the total sales amount for each product category where the total sales exceed $10,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000

natural_language: Find the total number of products ordered and total revenue generated from orders in the 'pending' status for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_ordered, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the segment-wise average order size (total amount) and the number of customers in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_size, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the names of employees and the assignments they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, o.order_id FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders placed on January 10, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date = '2023-01-10';

natural_language: Find customers who have made purchases from more than three distinct product categories, including their total spent and the number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Find the customers who have placed orders in multiple segments, along with the total number of unique segments they belong to.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.segment) AS unique_segments FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.segment) > 1

natural_language: List all orders that were made on a specific date.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-10-05';

natural_language: Retrieve all orders along with the names of the employees who processed them.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id;

natural_language: List all products and their total sales amount for those that have been sold in at least 20 orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id INNER JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 20

natural_language: List all products that have a price of $100 or more.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price >= 100;

natural_language: List all products with a name that starts with the letter 'S'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE 'S%';

natural_language: Get the average commission rate earned by employees based on the total sales they have made, only including those with sales over $1000.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Identify all customers who have placed more than 5 orders totaling more than $5,000, showing their names and order counts.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5 AND SUM(o.total_amount) > 5000

natural_language: Display the total sales for completed orders by each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) as total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all products with a price of exactly 30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 30;

natural_language: Find the average price and total quantity sold of products in the 'electronics' category for orders made by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS avg_price, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: Find the total order amount for products in the 'electronics' category that were sold by employees in the 'central' region.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND e.region = 'central';

natural_language: Retrieve the average product price grouped by category for products sold by employees in the 'central' region, but only include products that have generated total sales exceeding $5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' AND oi.quantity * p.price > 5000 GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Select products priced above $20 and under $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > 20 AND price < 100;

natural_language: Get the maximum price of products.
sql_query: SELECT MAX(price) AS max_product_price FROM products;

natural_language: Identify customers who have purchased the same product more than twice, including the total quantity purchased.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, oi.product_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.full_name, oi.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 2

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold for each order along with order IDs.
sql_query: SELECT oi.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_products_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY oi.order_id;

natural_language: Get the total amount spent by each customer along with the average order value and number of orders, focusing on customers who have spent more than $5,000 in total.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 5000

natural_language: Retrieve the list of products purchased by VIP customers along with the total amount spent by each customer on those products.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS amount_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY c.full_name, p.product_name;

natural_language: List the names of products that cost more than $20.
sql_query: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE cost > 20;

natural_language: Get the total quantity of products sold for each product, but only for products where total sales exceed 5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 5000

natural_language: Find all employees and the number of completed orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Identify the employee who has made the most sales and the associated total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold by each category, filtering for categories with total sales exceeding 500 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Get the number of products sold per product category for completed orders, filtering for categories with more than 100 units sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Get the names of retail customers from the east region who have completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date >= '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Count the number of distinct customers who have made orders of products from the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'furniture';

natural_language: Get the product names and their prices for all products costing less than $50.
sql_query: SELECT product_name, price FROM products WHERE price < 50;

natural_language: Generate a report that displays the year-over-year growth in total sales for the last 5 years.
sql_query: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) AS sales_year, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders o GROUP BY sales_year ORDER BY sales_year;

natural_language: Retrieve the average price of products sold in orders that are completed, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List customers and their respective order statuses for orders made in the month of January.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) = 1;

natural_language: Get all products that are in the 'Furniture' category and have a price greater than $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture' AND price > 200;

natural_language: List all unique products purchased by 'vip' customers who have completed more than 5 orders, along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: List all products sold by employees in the 'west' region, including the total quantity sold and the average selling price, sorted by average price.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY avg_price DESC;

natural_language: Get all products that belong to the 'furniture' category and cost less than $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture' AND cost < 200;

natural_language: Find all orders for customers located in a specific city.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Get the total cost of products sold in completed orders for retail customers along with the average number of products per order.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(p.cost * oi.quantity) AS total_cost, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_products_per_order FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Find all orders with a total amount greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Find the email addresses of customers who live in the city 'New York' and have made pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York' AND o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Calculate the average unit price of products sold through each employee, ensuring only completed orders are considered.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_unit_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Get the names of customers who have placed orders for the most expensive product in the catalog.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE oi.product_id = (SELECT product_id FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 1);

natural_language: Retrieve the product categories along with the count of products in each category that have been ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS product_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the most popular product category based on the number of items sold, but only include categories where the total items sold exceed 100.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Show the total amount earned by each employee from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_earned FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get all completed orders from the year 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-12-31';

natural_language: Calculate the average quantity of products sold per order in each customer segment, but only for segments with more than 5 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: List the full names of employees who have processed orders that were cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: List the order IDs and customer names for all orders placed after January 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date > '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Show all products with a price under $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < 30;

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total quantity sold across all orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Fetch the total amount of orders made by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Find the total amount spent by each customer in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the number of distinct products sold and total revenue generated in each city for retail segment customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS distinct_products, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: List all customers who have placed orders, along with their total order amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Show the order details for orders placed by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, orders.order_date FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get all orders that were placed in the month of December 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2023-12-01' AND '2023-12-31';

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and total sales amount for each city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Find the total number of orders and the total amount for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get total amount for all pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';

natural_language: Find the average price of products ordered by employees in the east region for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List employees who have processed more than 5 completed orders and their respective commission rates.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name, e.commission_rate HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5;

natural_language: Get the list of products that have been sold more than 100 times and their total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Determine the total revenue generated by each category of products where total sales exceed $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Get the total profit per product category for products sold in completed orders, only including categories with total profit greater than $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM((oi.unit_price - p.cost) * oi.quantity) AS total_profit FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM((oi.unit_price - p.cost) * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Determine the total quantity of products sold by each employee and return only those with more than 50 units sold.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Find the top 3 products by total revenue generated from orders with a status of 'completed'.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Retrieve the details of the top 3 products by quantity sold, including their respective categories and total revenue generated.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 3

natural_language: List all employees who have a commission rate of 15% or higher.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate >= 0.15;

natural_language: Find all employees with names containing 'a'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name LIKE '%a%';

natural_language: Show the total number of orders made by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of orders placed by each customer along with their email.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id GROUP BY customers.email;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of pending orders by city.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_pending FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total sales (amount spent) and display the employee who sold them the most.

natural_language: List the full names of customers and the total number of orders they have.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Identify the top 5 products sold to corporate customers by total revenue.

natural_language: List customers and their total expenditures who have made purchases in the 'east' region, showing only those with expenditures exceeding 2000.

natural_language: Determine the average price of products sold in the corporate segment and how many items contributed to that average.
sql_query:
SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_price, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_items_sold
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the average number of products per order, segmented by employee region.

sql_query: SELECT SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' AND customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have been sold to VIP customers, along with total quantities sold and revenue generated from those sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name

natural_language: Find the top 5 products with the highest total sales amount in completed orders, showing the product name and total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find the average order amount for each customer segment, including the total number of completed and cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Show the total revenue generated from completed orders for each city.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: Get the names of employees along with the total amount of orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_orders_processed FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the total expenses incurred in terms of product cost for completed orders segmented by employee region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_expenses FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.region

natural_language: Retrieve the number of orders and their total revenue from corporate customers that were completed by employees in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND e.region = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get all orders that were placed in the year 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2021;

natural_language: Find all products with a price between $20 and $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 20 AND 30;

natural_language: Calculate the total commissions for each employee based on the sales of products that cost less than $20.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(e.commission_rate * (oi.unit_price * oi.quantity)) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.cost < 20 GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered more than 10 times along with their total revenue generated.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Retrieve the number of orders and total sales for each product category sold to retail customers since 2022.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.order_date >= '2022-01-01' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Summarize total sales per product category for completed orders only, including only categories where total sales exceed $2000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: Determine the total sales generated by each product in the 'corporate' segment over the last 6 months.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 month' GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: List the categories of products that have generated more than $1000 in revenue in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Show the status of all orders along with the email addresses of the customers who made those orders.
sql_query: SELECT orders.status, customers.email FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id;

natural_language: List each product category with the total number of distinct products and the average price within that category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS total_products, AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List all customers who registered before March 1, 2019.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2019-03-01';

natural_language: Find the total commission earned by each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Count the number of orders with a total amount greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers from 'Los Angeles' who are in the VIP segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Los Angeles' AND segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Show all orders with total amounts between $50 and $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount BETWEEN 50 AND 200;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and total sales amount for each product category, restricting to categories with more than 15 orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 15

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who have an email containing 'example.com'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%example.com%';

natural_language: Find the full names of employees with a commission rate greater than 0.1.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM employees WHERE commission_rate > 0.1;

natural_language: Find the oldest customer in each segment who has made a purchase, along with their total spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, c.full_name, MIN(c.signup_date) AS oldest_signup_date, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment, c.full_name ORDER BY oldest_signup_date;

natural_language: Fetch the names of employees and the number of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) as orders_processed FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Fetch the top 3 products in terms of quantity sold to retail customers along with their total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Identify the most popular product along with its total revenue and the segments of customers who purchased it.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT c.segment, ',') AS customer_segments FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in completed orders and group by product name, displaying only those with an average price greater than 20.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING AVG(oi.unit_price) > 20

natural_language: Retrieve all order items with a unit price greater than $15.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price > 15;

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in completed orders by each employee in the 'central' region.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_product_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND e.region = 'central' GROUP BY e.full_name

natural_language: Count the total number of items sold in all orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(quantity) FROM order_items;

natural_language: Get the total number of pending orders for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS pending_orders FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the most popular product for each segment of customers based on total sales.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment, p.product_name ORDER BY c.segment, total_sales DESC

natural_language: Identify all the unique products purchased by customers in the 'vip' segment and count them.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS unique_products FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get all products priced between 10 and 50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 10 AND 50;

natural_language: Find the total number of items sold for each product, displayed with their names, only for those exceeding 50 units sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Count the number of products that have been sold by employees from the eastern region and total sales for those products, with sales above $700.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS products_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 700

natural_language: Retrieve all products priced at exactly $15.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 15;

natural_language: Get all customers who live in the city of 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM customers WHERE city = 'New York';

natural_language: Get the names of employees and the total amounts of their processed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) as total_orders FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: List the cities where corporate customers live and the number of orders they have placed.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: List all customers and their cities who have pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: List all orders with a total amount less than $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount < 20;

natural_language: Identify the top three cities with the highest revenue generated from orders, and list the respective total revenue, along with the number of unique customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get all products that have the name containing 'Phone'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Phone%';

natural_language: Find all pending orders for the customer with ID 3.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND customer_id = 3;

natural_language: Get the number of orders with status 'pending' for each product in the 'electronics' category, including product names and the quantity ordered, for orders made by 'corporate' customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, COUNT(o.order_id) AS pending_orders FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' AND c.segment = 'corporate' AND p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name

natural_language: Find all customers from the city 'New York' who have made any orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Show all completed orders made in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who registered before June 15, 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2021-06-15';

natural_language: Get the top 10 customers with the most recent signup date, including their full name and email.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c ORDER BY c.signup_date DESC LIMIT 10;

natural_language: Get customers who signed up after March 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2023-03-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of a specific order by order ID of 102.
sql_query: SELECT total_amount FROM orders WHERE order_id = 102;

natural_language: Show all customers who signed up in 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2020;

natural_language: Find the total quantity of products sold for each category in completed orders, filtering for categories with total quantity sold over 200.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 200

natural_language: Find the average order amount from customers who have made more than three completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) > 3)

natural_language: Calculate the total cost of products sold by each employee for pending orders.
