sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Determine the total number of unique customers who have ordered in each segment, along with the total revenue generated from each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS unique_customers, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of orders placed by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_vip_spent FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Retrieve the names of employees who have processed orders greater than $10,000 in total, along with the total sales they achieved.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Calculate the total costs versus total revenue for each product category, showing only those categories where total revenue exceeds total costs.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_costs FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost)

natural_language: Get the details of employees who have not processed any orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Get the list of products with their total sales amount and number sold, for products that have sold more than $1000 in total.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Calculate the total costs incurred by each customer segment for all completed orders, and analyze which segment has the highest costs based on the cost of products sold.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY total_cost DESC

natural_language: Find the customers who have placed more than 5 orders and calculate the total amount spent by each of them.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Retrieve a list of all products along with the average number of items sold and total revenue generated from those products, but only consider products that were part of completed orders by customers from the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id

natural_language: Fetch the employee names and their commission rates for those who have processed completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT e.full_name, e.commission_rate FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the average price of products ordered by customers from the 'VIP' segment, along with their full names.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, AVG(p.price) AS average_product_price FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: List the customers who have spent more than $2000, including their segment and signup date.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, c.signup_date, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 2000

natural_language: Generate a list of order IDs and their status for orders placed by 'vip' customers.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Show the total number of orders for each customer in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: List all customers who signed up in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= '2023-01-01' AND signup_date < '2024-01-01';

natural_language: Retrieve all order items for a specific product with product_id 10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE product_id = 10;

natural_language: Get the total price of all products in the Electronics category.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(price) as total_price FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics';

natural_language: Get products with a price less than $30 or a cost less than $15.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < 30 OR cost < 15;

natural_language: Find the names of employees and the average total amount of orders they handled.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the list of products with their total sales amount and the number of times they were sold, only for orders that are completed and made by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS times_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Find the total costs of products sold per category, but only include categories with total costs exceeding $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) > 1000

natural_language: Get the names and signup dates of corporate customers who have made orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get all orders that were placed in the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 day';

natural_language: Find the customer details and their most recent order status, ordered by their signup date.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, o.status FROM customers c LEFT JOIN (SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) recent ON c.customer_id = recent.customer_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON recent.customer_id = o.customer_id AND recent.last_order_date = o.order_date ORDER BY c.signup_date;

natural_language: Get the total number of items sold and the total revenue for each product category, but only for products with a revenue greater than $2000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 2000

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue and the number of orders for each customer segment, showing only segments with a total revenue greater than a specified threshold.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Identify which products have a higher total sales volume than the average sales volume of all products in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > (SELECT AVG(total_units) FROM (SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY oi.product_id) AS avg_subquery)

natural_language: Determine the highest selling product in terms of total revenue for each category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category, p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

natural_language: List every product along with the total sales amount and the number of orders it appears in, but only for products sold in the retail segment where total sales exceed $2000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 2000

natural_language: List all products that have a cost greater than $5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > 5;

natural_language: Calculate the total sales and the number of products sold for each employee from the west region, including only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE e.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Identify the employees whose total sales exceed $50,000 and the average order value they have worked on.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 50000

natural_language: List all pending orders placed in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of completed orders along with the respective employee names.
sql_query: SELECT orders.total_amount, employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get a list of customers with their order status who have placed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all products that cost less than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost < 50;

natural_language: Find all employees with a commission rate greater than 0.1.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate > 0.1;

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue and average quantity sold per product for all products sold to corporate customers, filtering for products with total revenue over $2000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 2000

natural_language: Find the latest orders made by each customer along with the order statuses.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_date, orders.status FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE (customers.customer_id, orders.order_date) IN (SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_date) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id);

natural_language: Retrieve the total revenue generated by each product category from completed orders, filtering for categories with total revenue over $20,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 20000

natural_language: Retrieve employees along with the count of their pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS pending_orders FROM employees LEFT JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Find all products with a cost of $5 or less.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost <= 5;

natural_language: Show the total amount spent by each customer along with their city.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: Retrieve all products that were ordered more than 10 times, along with their prices.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, p.price HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10;

natural_language: Find the order dates and statuses of orders from customers in the city of 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_date, o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Find the full names of employees and the total amount of orders they processed that are pending.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_pending FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total sales where the sales are from eastern region employees only.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List the categories of products that have been sold to both 'retail' and 'corporate' customers, along with the number of distinct customers from each segment who have purchased those categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.segment = 'retail' THEN c.customer_id END) AS retail_customers, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.segment = 'corporate' THEN c.customer_id END) AS corporate_customers FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) > 1

natural_language: List the average unit price of products sold by each product category where the total number of orders of that category exceeds 10.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_unit_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: Get the total sales amount for each product, showing only those products with sales higher than $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Retrieve the highest-selling product's name and total sales amount, considering only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List all orders placed on '2023-01-01'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Find the most popular product in each city based on the total quantity sold, but only include cities that have sold more than 100 units of products.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.city, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Get the total amount of orders placed by customers in 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE city = 'New York');

natural_language: Get the average number of items per completed order for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_items_per_order FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Get the average amount of orders placed by each customer grouped by segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold and the average order total for orders placed by 'vip' customers, only for those orders where the total amount exceeds $1000.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_products_sold, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Find the total amount spent by each corporate customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the product names that have generated more than $5000 in total sales, along with their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Determine the average quantity of products sold per order for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_quantity_per_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Identify the products that have never been sold and the number of orders that include each product, along with customer segments.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count, c.segment FROM products AS p LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.product_name, c.segment HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) = 0

natural_language: List the total amount of orders grouped by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_segment_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List the customers and their order details for orders that have been cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_id, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue from products in the 'electronics' category, grouped by month, for completed orders only.
sql_query: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) AS order_month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date);

natural_language: Retrieve the number of orders and their statuses for customers who live in the city of 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York' GROUP BY c.full_name, o.status;

natural_language: Get the count of products sold for each product in the 'electronics' category, where total units sold exceed 50.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: List employees with the total commissions earned from orders with a status of 'pending'.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Calculate the average order amount for each customer segment, but include only the customers who have ordered more than once.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1

natural_language: Get the average revenue per order by customer segment and order status.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, o.status, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment, o.status;

natural_language: Get the highest priced product sold by employees in a specific region along with the employee’s name.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, MAX(p.price) AS highest_product_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders along with the corresponding customer names and emails for customers located in New York.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name, c.email FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Show the names of customers along with the orders they made that are currently pending.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Find all customers from Los Angeles who signed up in 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Los Angeles' AND signup_date BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-12-31';

natural_language: Get the details of orders including customer name and order amount for orders over $500.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Find the average cost of products sold in each order where the total order amount exceeds $200.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, AVG(p.cost) AS average_product_cost FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY o.order_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 200

natural_language: Get all completed orders with a total amount between $100 and $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount BETWEEN 100 AND 200;

natural_language: Identify which products have been sold in more than 5 different orders and return the total revenue for each of those products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: List the customers who have ordered products in more than three different categories and the count of those categories.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Show employees from the 'east' region along with the orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, o.order_id FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east';

natural_language: Retrieve the total quantity of products sold per category from completed orders, only for products costing less than 50.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.cost < 50 AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the most sold product among all customers and the total number of times it was sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sold DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Calculate the total amount spent by customers in each city who have placed at least one order for products priced over $100, providing a count of such customers per city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS total_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.price > 100 GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Get the names of all products that have a cost lower than their price.
sql_query: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE cost < price;

natural_language: Find all customers who have placed completed orders and live in the city of 'San Francisco'.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.city = 'San Francisco';

natural_language: Get a list of employees and the number of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the emails of customers who have more than one order placed.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.customer_id HAVING COUNT(orders.order_id) > 1;

natural_language: Count the number of different products ordered by each customer, filtering to those with more than 2 distinct products.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_product_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 2

natural_language: List all employees with their commission rates and the total amounts of the orders they handled.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_handled FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate;

natural_language: List all completed orders from the month of March.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 3;

natural_language: Total sales by product category for the last six months, filtering out categories with total sales below $3000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 MONTH' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) >= 3000

natural_language: Get a list of all products sold to VIP customers that generated more than $1,000 in total revenue, including the product names and total revenue for each.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Find the customer with the highest total spending, including their full name and city.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.city, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.city ORDER BY total_spending DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Show all order items for a specific order with ID 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 5;

natural_language: List the employee and the total number of completed orders they handled, grouped by segments with at least 3 completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name, c.segment HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3

natural_language: Get a count of products in each order.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(oi.product_id) as product_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id;

natural_language: Find the total number of orders in each segment category.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Identify customers who ordered more than 5 different products and their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS product_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 5

natural_language: Find all orders with a total amount greater than 1000.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Retrieve all employees with a commission rate of 0.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate = 0;

natural_language: Find the total amount spent by each customer in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the number of products sold and total revenue generated for each product category for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get all products that are priced under $30 and belong to the 'home' category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < 30 AND category = 'home';

natural_language: Get the total number of items ordered and total revenue generated from corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_ordered, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Identify the top 3 products by revenue generated from completed orders taken by employees in the west region.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold per category where the total revenue exceeds $1,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Determine which product has the highest average price, but only include products that have been sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY avg_price DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get all incomplete orders.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status != 'completed';

natural_language: Calculate the total cost of orders per city, considering only orders above $1000, and group them by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.segment, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.total_amount > 1000 GROUP BY c.city, c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders placed in June 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 6 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: Get a list of completed orders along with the corresponding customer names.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.full_name FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the total sales amount for each customer by segment, including only those who have made at least three orders and have a total spent greater than $1000.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) >= 3) GROUP BY c.segment, c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Get the total sales amount for each region based on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Find the average number of items per completed order per employee, only include employees with more than 3 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(item_count) AS avg_items_per_order FROM (SELECT o.employee_id, o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS item_count FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id) AS order_summary JOIN employees AS e ON order_summary.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(order_summary.order_id) > 3

natural_language: Get the total sales amount for each product category, but only if that category has sold more than 500 items.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Retrieve all order statuses for orders placed in March 2023.
sql_query: SELECT status FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2023-03-01' AND '2023-03-31';

natural_language: Get the average total amount of completed orders by segment type.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get a breakdown of total sales from completed orders by product category and segment of the customer.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category, c.segment;

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total sales amount, including their category, and display total sales only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Show all products in the 'furniture' category with a price below $300.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture' AND price < 300;

natural_language: Get a summary of total revenue and average order amount by region for employees who have sold more than 20 products.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.region HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 20

natural_language: List each customer's full name and their total spending, ordered by spending in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name ORDER BY total_spending DESC;

natural_language: Determine the product with the highest profit margin and its respective category, but only if it has been sold more than 15 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, (SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost)) AS profit_margin FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 15 ORDER BY profit_margin DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Get all order items that have a unit price less than $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price < 20;

natural_language: Retrieve the average order value for each city, including the total number of customers in each city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS total_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city

natural_language: Find all order items with a quantity greater than 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE quantity > 5;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and average order value from customers in the VIP segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Find the total sales made by each employee along with their commission rate.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales, employees.commission_rate FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate;

natural_language: Find the products that were sold the most (by quantity) in orders taken by employees from a specific region, along with total earnings.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_earnings FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_quantity DESC;

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and total sales amount for each employee, only including employees who have sold more than $2,000 in total.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 2000

natural_language: Get the full names of all employees earning a commission rate greater than 5%.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM employees WHERE commission_rate > 0.05;

natural_language: List the total amount of orders along with the details of the corresponding employee for all cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT o.total_amount, e.full_name FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: List products that have been ordered more than 10 times and their total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: Determine the average price of products in the 'clothing' category that have been sold in completed orders, grouped by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(p.price) AS avg_price FROM products p INNER JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE p.category = 'clothing' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find all products in the 'electronics' category that cost more than $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'electronics' AND price > 100;

natural_language: Get the number of unique customers who made orders grouped by employee, including the total order count for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS unique_customers, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Identify the top 5 cities with the highest average spending per order.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY average_spending DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Retrieve the order status and total amount for orders placed by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated by each customer segment and display only segments that generate over $1000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Find all customers who signed up on a specific date.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date = '2023-10-01';

natural_language: List all products sold to each segment of customers along with the quantity sold and the total revenue generated from those sales.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment, p.product_id, p.product_name

natural_language: List all products that are currently available.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_id IS NOT NULL;

natural_language: List the total number of products sold per order.
sql_query: SELECT order_items.order_id, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_products FROM order_items JOIN orders ON order_items.order_id = orders.order_id GROUP BY order_items.order_id;

natural_language: Get the count of orders made by each customer segment along with the total amounts.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id), SUM(o.total_amount) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve completed orders along with the employee name who processed them.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, e.full_name FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the total amount spent by each customer along with their full name.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) as total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: List the segments and their total revenue, including only those segments that account for more than 25% of total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS segment_revenue FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT 0.25 * SUM(total_amount) FROM orders)

natural_language: Get the total quantity sold by product for products with a total quantity sold greater than 100.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Identify the employee who has the highest total sales from completed orders, along with a breakdown of their sales by product category.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name, p.category ORDER BY total_sales DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY

natural_language: Get a list of products that have been ordered more than 10 times, along with their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_orders FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: Find the average cost of products sold in orders that are pending, grouped by order status.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, AVG(p.cost) AS avg_product_cost FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: List the product names and their total sales amount for products sold by employees in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Show a summary of total order amounts by segment for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find all completed orders made in the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 day';

natural_language: Find the total revenue generated from each product that has a price above the average price of all products, sold to retail customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE p.price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products) AND c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name;

natural_language: List all products that have a price of $0.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 0;

natural_language: Retrieve the average order amount and total number of orders for each product category where the average order amount exceeds $100.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 100

natural_language: Find customers who have placed more than 5 orders, and show their name, email, and city.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Show the top 3 customers by total spending along with their segment and total orders placed.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.segment ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get a report on the total number of orders and the shared average price of products for each employee, where the average price exceeds $50.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_product_price FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING AVG(oi.unit_price) > 50

natural_language: Identify the products which were ordered at least once in each customer segment, showing product names and the segments.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, c.segment FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.product_name, c.segment HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.segment) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT segment) FROM customers);

natural_language: List all unique customers who have placed orders in every segment (retail, corporate, vip) and count their orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.segment) = 3

natural_language: Get all customers who are in the 'corporate' segment and live in 'Chicago'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND city = 'Chicago';

natural_language: Retrieve the employee names and regions for all employees who processed orders in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east';

natural_language: Calculate the total cost of products sold by each employee, but only for those employees who have made sales exceeding $10,000 in total sales.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Get all orders made between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31';

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who have completed orders along with their order totals.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the number of orders per product along with the total sales for those products, but only include products with over 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: Get all employees from the east region with a commission rate lower than 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'east' AND commission_rate < 0.05;

natural_language: List employees in 'east' region who have sold products totaling more than $5000 and count their distinct customers.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: List each customer with the total number of items they ordered, focusing on those who have ordered more than 15 items overall.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 15

natural_language: Find the average commission earned by employees based on the total sales of their orders, sorting the results from highest to lowest.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, AVG(e.commission_rate * o.total_amount) AS average_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY average_commission DESC;

natural_language: Count the number of orders with a 'pending' status.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get the average commission rate of employees selling products from each category, only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Fetch the emails and signup dates of VIP customers who have orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.email, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Retrieve products priced at exactly $25.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 25;

natural_language: Find the average quantity of products sold per order for completed orders, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_quantity FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve orders that were created after the start of 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Get the maximum order value for each employee along with the corresponding customer's full name and their segment.
sql_query:
SELECT e.full_name AS employee_name, c.full_name AS customer_name, c.segment, MAX(o.total_amount) AS max_order_value
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id
GROUP BY e.full_name, c.full_name, c.segment;

natural_language: Find all order items that have a quantity greater than 10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE quantity > 10;

natural_language: Retrieve all products that belong to the 'Home Appliances' category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Home Appliances';

natural_language: Get the highest selling product categories along with total sales amount, only considering orders from corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) as total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_sales DESC;

natural_language: List the products sold by customers from the 'vip' segment, along with the count of each product sold, sorted by the quantity sold in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY quantity_sold DESC

natural_language: Show all orders that have an order date in March 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2023-03-01' AND '2023-03-31';

natural_language: Calculate the average order value for each customer segment and compare it with the overall average order value across all segments.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment; SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders;

natural_language: List products that have been ordered by VIP customers and their total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Get the total count of products sold and their total revenue for each product category, ensuring categories with revenue exceeding 2000 are included.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total sales, including the total units sold for each product and which employee sold the most of each product during the past quarter.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold, e.full_name AS best_selling_employee FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 month' GROUP BY p.product_id, e.employee_id ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Show all completed orders placed by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate');

natural_language: Retrieve the total costs incurred by each employee, along with their name, where the total costs exceed $5000, filtered by the 'central' region.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_costs FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) > 5000

natural_language: Find all employees who have processed more than five completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5;

natural_language: List the average product price and total sales in the last year for each product category, excluding categories with less than 1000 total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS avg_price, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 YEAR' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Display the employee names and their commission rates for orders that have a total amount greater than 100.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.total_amount > 100;

natural_language: Find the total sales amount for each product sold, only if that product's total sales amount exceeds $5000, and group by category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Find the average cost of products sold in completed orders for each customer segment in 2023.
sql_query:
SELECT c.segment, AVG(p.cost) AS average_product_cost 
FROM order_items oi 
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id 
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id 
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id 
WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2023 
GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the email addresses of customers from the 'vip' segment who have pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip' AND orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get the names and cities of customers who placed orders in the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name, customers.city FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days';

natural_language: Retrieve all pending orders that were created in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND order_date > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Get the names of all VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Identify the top three products by total sales amount in orders from VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Count the number of orders placed by each customer.
sql_query: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

natural_language: List the employees who have sold products from more than three different categories, along with the count of categories.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Get all products that have a price of $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 100;

natural_language: Get all employees from the 'central' region with a commission rate of 10%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'central' AND commission_rate = 0.10;

natural_language: Get the total sales and average order amount for each customer segment, including the number of completed and cancelled orders, ordered by total sales in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY total_sales DESC;

natural_language: Get all orders with customer details for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.full_name, c.email FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List the employee names along with the total commission they earned based on orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount * employees.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total amount of orders per customer along with their email addresses.
sql_query: SELECT c.email, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Get the top three products by total sales amount for the corporate segment customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales amount for completed orders grouped by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the average price of products in each category.
sql_query: SELECT products.category, AVG(products.price) AS average_price FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id GROUP BY products.category;

natural_language: Find all orders with a status of 'cancelled' and total amount less than 100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND total_amount < 100;

natural_language: List customers from the corporate segment along with their signup date and total order amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY c.full_name, c.signup_date;

natural_language: Retrieve a list of all employees in the central region with completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'central' AND orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get a list of all orders along with the names of the corresponding employees.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, e.full_name FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the total revenue from 'corporate' customers in the 'east' region, grouped by employee, only including employees who have earned more than $1000 in commissions.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND c.city = 'east' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) > 1000

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and total revenue for each city segmented by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city, c.segment;

natural_language: List the total number of products sold by each region, but only include regions where the total quantity sold exceeds 150.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.region HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 150

natural_language: List all customers from Chicago who signed up after 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chicago' AND signup_date > '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Get all products with a price between $30 and $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 30 AND 100;

natural_language: List all employees along with the total number of completed orders they've processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_completed_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the details of orders made by customers in 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Get the average commission rate for employees who have processed more than the average order amount.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission_rate FROM employees e JOIN (SELECT employee_id, AVG(total_amount) as average_order_amount FROM orders GROUP BY employee_id) AS avg_orders ON e.employee_id = avg_orders.employee_id WHERE avg_orders.average_order_amount > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders)

natural_language: List all orders placed on '2023-10-10'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-10-10';

natural_language: Find all products whose names contain 'Chair'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Chair%';

natural_language: Fetch all products that belong to the 'clothing' category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'clothing';

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of products sold per employee, filtering for employees with more than 20 products sold.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Determine the top 3 most frequently sold products, their total quantity sold, and total revenue, per customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment, p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 3

natural_language: Determine the average order value for each product category, filtering out categories with less than $1,000 in total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have a price between 10 and 40.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 10 AND 40;

natural_language: Show each product's total sold quantity and total sales amount, but only for products whose total sales exceed $10000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 10000

natural_language: Find all employees along with the orders they are responsible for.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name AS employee_name, o.order_id FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all segments of customers who signed up after January 2022.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT segment FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2022-01-31';

natural_language: List all employees who have a full_name containing 'Smith'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name LIKE '%Smith%';

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in orders that were completed in January 2023, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get all orders with a total amount between $50 and $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount BETWEEN 50 AND 100;

natural_language: Get the names of all products priced less than or equal to $15.
sql_query: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE price <= 15;

natural_language: Count the number of completed orders for each product and show only those products that have more than 20 orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 20

natural_language: Fetch all completed orders with a total amount of exactly $250.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount = 250;

natural_language: Get all pending orders with an order date in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: List all completed orders along with the customer names who made them.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the average cost per product category sold by employees from the 'west' region, showing the category and average cost.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.cost) AS average_cost FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Retrieve the total quantity sold for each product in the 'electronics' category, but only include products that have been sold more than 20 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Get the total order value and count of orders for each product sold by employees in the 'west' region.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_order_value FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Identify each customer segment and the number of unique products purchased, only including segments with more than 3 unique products sold.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 3

natural_language: List the top 5 products with the highest total sales from completed orders, along with their respective total sales amounts.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find all order items with a unit price of exactly $25.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price = 25;

natural_language: Get all products that have been ordered along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get a list of customers who live in Los Angeles and signed up before 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Los Angeles' AND signup_date < '2021-01-01';

natural_language: Get the list of customers and their total spending on orders, grouped by customer ID.
