sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name;

natural_language: List the order IDs and total amounts for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the names of employees who have processed more than 10 orders, along with their total commission earned from those orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_processed, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 10

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of products and their total sales amounts for each order.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id;

natural_language: Find all products that have been ordered by customers in the VIP segment, along with the total quantity sold and the total revenue generated from these products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the name of the customer who made the largest single order and the total amount of that order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.total_amount = (SELECT MAX(total_amount) FROM orders);

natural_language: List all orders placed in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Find the average total amount of orders for each product category, considering only completed orders made by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the full name and region of employees who have processed pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, employees.region FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get all orders that were made on or before '2023-07-01'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date <= '2023-07-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the employee who sold the most expensive single product along with the customer who bought it.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name AS employee_name, c.full_name AS customer_name, MAX(p.price) AS highest_product_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY e.full_name, c.full_name ORDER BY highest_product_price DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve the customers who have the highest total spent amount but have only 2 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) = (SELECT MAX(total_spent) FROM (SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, c.customer_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 2) AS subquery);

natural_language: Get the highest and lowest order total for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, MAX(o.total_amount) AS highest_order, MIN(o.total_amount) AS lowest_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List customers who have made orders but have not yet signed up for VIP segment.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment <> 'vip';

natural_language: Retrieve the names of all products sold in orders placed by corporate customers, along with the total quantity sold for each product.
sql_query:
SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold 
FROM order_items oi 
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id 
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id 
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id 
WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' 
GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List all products sold in 'central' region along with the total quantity sold, but only include those with total sales exceeding 50 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Count the number of unique customers that have ordered each product, showing only those products with more than 2 distinct customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) > 2

natural_language: Get the list of cities with the number of customers in each segment along with the average order amount for orders from that city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.segment, COUNT(c.customer_id) AS customer_count, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city, c.segment

natural_language: Find all employees who have sold products that were ordered with a total amount greater than $2000, along with the count of those products.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS products_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.total_amount > 2000 GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: List the customers who have made more than 5 orders, including their total order amount and the date of their latest order.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order_date FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Get all customers that signed up in the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days';

natural_language: Find the total amount spent by corporate customers on products from a specific category.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND p.category = 'electronics';

natural_language: Get customers who signed up in 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31';

natural_language: Retrieve the names of customers along with their respective order IDs where the order status is 'pending'.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_id FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: List products that have been ordered more than 50 times and calculate their average sold price.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_sold_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 50

natural_language: List all products along with their total sales in the corporate segment customers, grouping by product.
sql_query:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.segment = 'corporate'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name;

natural_language: Find the average order value in the corporate segment for orders processed by employees in the central region, alongside the count of unique products sold.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_sold FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND e.region = 'central';

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales generated by each segment of customers, along with the count of unique customers in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List all products purchased in the last month, with each product's name and the total quantity sold, only including those with sales above 20 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 MONTH' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Find the products that have a total sales count greater than 100, including their average sale price.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sales_count, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_sale_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Get the count of completed and cancelled orders for each employee.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(CASE WHEN orders.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_count, COUNT(CASE WHEN orders.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_count FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get all orders made on December 25, 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2022-12-25';

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders made in the month of September 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date BETWEEN '2023-09-01' AND '2023-09-30';

natural_language: Find the top three customers by total spending, including their segment and the total amount they have spent on orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.segment ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get the average total amount of completed orders for each retail customer.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, AVG(orders.total_amount) AS average_order FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'retail' AND orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: List all completed orders with a total amount greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount > 500;

natural_language: List the names and prices of all products costing less than $20.
sql_query: SELECT product_name, price FROM products WHERE price < 20;

natural_language: Show the total sales by product name for products that have sold more than 50 units in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Get the total quantity sold of each product and their average selling price across completed orders placed by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name

natural_language: Get all orders placed after January 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Find the average quantity of products ordered by customers in the 'VIP' segment who reside in 'Chicago'.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_quantity FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.city = 'Chicago' AND c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Retrieve the names of employees who have completed orders along with the order dates.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, o.order_date FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the names of customers and the count of their pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS pending_orders_count FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all products with names containing 'Pro'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Pro%';

natural_language: Get all completed orders placed after June 1, 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date > '2021-06-01';

natural_language: List the percentage of completed vs cancelled orders for each city, based on the total number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_percentage, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(o.order_id) AS cancelled_percentage FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered more than 100 times, along with their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Get all orders made before last year.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date < '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the product names and their prices alongside the corresponding order item quantities.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.price, oi.quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

natural_language: List all orders that have a status of 'pending' or 'completed'.
sql_query: SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE status IN ('pending', 'completed');

natural_language: Get the total number of customers in each city, distinguishing between retail and corporate segments.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.segment, COUNT(c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers c GROUP BY c.city, c.segment;

natural_language: List all orders made by customers with the email domain 'gmail.com'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE email LIKE '%@gmail.com');

natural_language: List all products with a cost between $10 and $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost BETWEEN 10 AND 50;

natural_language: List the product names and their categories that have never been ordered, along with the count of their respective orders (which will be zero).
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) = 0

natural_language: Show all customers who signed up more than a year ago.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year';

natural_language: List all products priced between $20 and $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 20 AND 100;

natural_language: Find the employees who have the highest commission rate and the number of completed orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders_count FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name, e.commission_rate ORDER BY e.commission_rate DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve the commission rates and names of employees who sold more than $10,000 in total.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.commission_rate HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000;

natural_language: Identify customers who have ordered products from more than 2 different categories, along with their total spent and signup date.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, c.signup_date FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 2

natural_language: Count how many products have been sold more than 10 times and list their names along with total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 products sold by total revenue in the east region, along with the total units sold for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find which employees have processed orders over a certain total amount.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name HAVING SUM(orders.total_amount) > 1000;

natural_language: Calculate the total products sold per segment and the total revenue generated from those sales.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Identify the products with the highest total sales, but only show products that sold more than 100 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: List the cities and signup dates of customers who have pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 products by total sales amount, including the total sales and number of orders for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Show the employee names and order counts for pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS pending_order_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Identify which products made losses and by how much, broken down by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, p.product_name, (SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost)) AS loss FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category, p.product_name HAVING (SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost)) < 0

natural_language: Determine which products have not been sold in the last year, and their respective prices and categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.price, p.category FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Determine the total sales amount for each product in the 'electronics' category, only showing products that have been sold more than 50 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Find the average order total for each product category and how many times each product was ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_ordered FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Count how many customers are in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT segment, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY segment;

natural_language: List the names of customers and the order dates of their most recent order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(o.order_date) as most_recent_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Show the total amount of orders by region (segment) for retail customers.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_retail_sales FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: Calculate the total quantity of products sold by VIP customers and get the list of products that have total sales greater than 50.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of items ordered and their associated amounts for all orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_amount FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who signed up in the year 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= '2021-01-01' AND signup_date < '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Get a list of all products ordered more than once by their respective categories.
sql_query: SELECT products.category, products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_ordered FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.category, products.product_name HAVING SUM(order_items.quantity) > 1

natural_language: Get the number of distinct products sold and the total revenue generated from these products for each city, only considering orders that have been completed.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS distinct_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Retrieve the full name of employees who processed cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: List all products that cost less than $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost < 20;

natural_language: Show all customers who registered in April 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2023-04-01' AND '2023-04-30';

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and the total revenue generated from orders in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(oi.product_id) AS total_products_sold, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed'

natural_language: Find customers who have purchased products from at least two different categories, and their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) >= 2

natural_language: Retrieve products that cost between $20 and $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost BETWEEN 20 AND 100;

natural_language: Show all order items that have a unit price of $15.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price = 15;

natural_language: Get the total revenue for products in the 'electronics' category for orders placed by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have been sold in orders totaling over $1000, including their name and total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: List all completed orders from the last week.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days';

natural_language: Show all orders placed in the month of March.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 3;

natural_language: Get a summary of the total number of orders and total sales for each customer segment, including those with pending and cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the product that has the highest average sale price in completed orders grouped by customer segments.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, c.segment, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_sale_price FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name, c.segment ORDER BY avg_sale_price DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get all employees with a commission rate of 10%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate = 0.10;

natural_language: Get the total spending by each customer in different segments, filtering those who have spent more than the average.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment, c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM (SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id) AS customer_totals)

natural_language: List all orders that were placed in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Find the customer with the highest total spending on completed orders for products in the 'Electronics' category, and return their name, email, and total spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY total_spending DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: List the top three products by total sales amount and the number of distinct customers who purchased them.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Retrieve the names of customers who have made purchases over $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Identify the employees with the least sales volume, showing their name, region, and the total sales made.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY total_sales ASC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Retrieve customers who have not placed any orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.order_id IS NULL;

natural_language: List all customers who signed up in March 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) = 3 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2022;

natural_language: Retrieve the total spending by each customer in the eastern region, filtering out those who spent less than 500.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) >= 500

natural_language: Find the average order total for each segment of customers and the maximum order amount within each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total, MAX(o.total_amount) AS max_order_total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Show all orders with their corresponding customer segments.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.segment FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

natural_language: Show the top 5 products sold in the last quarter based on the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 month' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List all completed orders and their statuses for VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the total revenue from completed orders grouped by city.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: Get all customers who signed up after January 1, 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2020-01-01';

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold by category, but only for categories that generated more than $1000 in total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Fetch the order IDs and their total amounts for orders placed after a specific date.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.order_date > '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Identify the customers in the corporate segment who have ordered products costing more than $100 in the last year.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND p.price > 100 AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year';

natural_language: List all products with average price above $300 that have been sold by any employee during the last year.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 YEAR' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING AVG(p.price) > 300

natural_language: Retrieve the top 3 products with the highest sales total, including product names and their respective sales amounts.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get all products with the name containing 'Laptop'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Laptop%';

natural_language: List the top 5 customers by total order amount and their average order value, along with the number of orders they made.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name ORDER BY total_order_amount DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Find all customers in the corporate segment who have an email.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND email IS NOT NULL;

natural_language: Identify all customers who have placed orders without purchasing any products from a specific category in the last two years.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category != 'specific_category' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '2 year' GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who signed up after January 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Find all customers who joined in the month of June 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2023-06-01' AND '2023-06-30';

natural_language: Get all products that have a price between $20 and $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 20 AND 50;

natural_language: Find all customers who signed up before January 1, 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Count the number of completed orders for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Find all cities with customers that have ordered products from more than 5 different categories.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 5;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of orders along with the full name of employees who handled those orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get a list of customers who have ordered products from at least 3 different categories.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) >= 3

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount spent by each customer in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Get the product categories along with the total number of products in each category that have been ordered at least once.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS total_products FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Retrieve the cities of all customers in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT city FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Identify the top three most expensive products sold by employees from the 'east' region in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND e.region = 'east' ORDER BY p.price DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get the total number of order items for employees in the west region, but only for orders that are completed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE e.region = 'west' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Determine the number of different products ordered by each customer segment, showing the segment and the product count.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS product_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the total sales for each product category where the total sales exceed $10,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000

natural_language: Get total revenue generated by each product in the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id WHERE products.category = 'furniture' GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the segment with the highest average order value and the number of orders placed in that segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in each region by employees, considering only completed orders, and display the region and average price.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Show the total spending by customers in different cities.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Get a count of the orders made by corporate segment customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get all completed orders made after March 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date > '2023-03-01';

natural_language: Determine the total sales for each segment for the last year and compare it to the previous year, and calculate the growth percentage.
sql_query: SELECT current.segment, current.total_sales AS current_sales, previous.total_sales AS previous_sales, ((current.total_sales - previous.total_sales) / previous.total_sales) * 100 AS growth_percentage FROM (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' AND o.order_date < CURRENT_DATE GROUP BY c.segment) AS current JOIN (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '2 year' AND o.order_date < CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' GROUP BY c.segment) AS previous ON current.segment = previous.segment

natural_language: Find the highest selling product along with its category in the west region.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY total_sold DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: List all employees along with the total sales generated by each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the average order value for each customer segment and the percentage of customers in each segment that have placed at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(customer_id) FROM customers) AS percentage_of_customers FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find employees who have processed orders in more than 3 different cities.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.city) AS city_count FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.city) > 3

natural_language: Get the top 3 products by total revenue and the segments that bought them.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, STRING_AGG(DISTINCT c.segment, ',') AS customer_segments FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 products by total sales amount for the central region employees, including their commission earnings from those sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Identify any customers who have only placed one order, and report their full name, order total, and order date.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.total_amount, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) = 1)

natural_language: Show all customers from the city 'Miami' who are VIP.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Miami' AND segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get the total order value for completed orders grouped by employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_value FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Get the list of products that have never been ordered.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name FROM products LEFT JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id WHERE order_items.product_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Find the top 5 customers by total order amount and display their details along with the total amount they have spent.
sql_query:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.email, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.email
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find all completed orders from a specific employee with employee_id 2.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND employee_id = 2;

natural_language: Identify product categories that have generated sales above $3000, along with the total sales and number of products sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(oi.product_id) AS total_products_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 3000

natural_language: List the email addresses of customers who have made any pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated by each employee based on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the top products that have the highest average selling price in completed orders, filtering only for those products sold in retail segment orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_selling_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY average_selling_price DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List products that have been ordered more than 20 times, along with the total revenue generated for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Show the total number of products sold by each employee in the east region, including the employee name and total products sold, for completed orders only.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE e.region = 'east' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Show all products that are in the 'home' category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'home';

natural_language: Get the list of employees who have sold products in multiple categories and the number of unique categories they've sold.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS unique_categories FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 1

natural_language: Retrieve the names of products that generated more than 1000 in total revenue, including the total revenue for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Get the total sales amount for each product category where the total sales exceeded $1,000, including only completed orders from customers in the VIP segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: List products that have been sold in more than three different orders and show their total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 3

natural_language: Fetch the total number of items sold and the average sale price for products in the 'Electronics' category from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_sale_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get a count of orders and their total amounts for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List the total amount spent by each customer along with their city.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.city, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Get all products that are priced between $10 and $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 10 AND 100;

natural_language: Find the total amount spent by customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip');

natural_language: Find all completed orders along with the names of the employees who handled them.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, orders.order_date, employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the top 3 products by total sales amount, including their category.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: List all products sold in the cancelled orders along with the reason for cancellation.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS cancellation_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 0

natural_language: Find the most popular product category for each customer segment, including the number of orders placed for that category.
sql_query:
SELECT c.segment, p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY c.segment, p.category
ORDER BY order_count DESC;

natural_language: Get the list of customers who have ordered products in the 'electronics' category, including their total number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Find the customers who have a total order count greater than 5 and have the highest single order value.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, MAX(o.total_amount) AS highest_order FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5 ORDER BY highest_order DESC

natural_language: Get a summary of total orders, total amount, and average amount for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 products by total revenue generated in the 'books' category.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'books' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who joined before December 31, 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2020-12-31';

natural_language: Find the total commission earned by each employee from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Show the most popular product based on the number of times it has been ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS times_ordered FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY times_ordered DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Identify all employees who have generated more than $10,000 in sales, including their full name, region, and the total amount they have generated.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated from orders that contain products from the category 'Electronics' for corporate customers in the last quarter.
sql_query:
SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 month' AND p.category = 'Electronics';

natural_language: List all employees with 'Manager' in their title.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name LIKE '%Manager%';

natural_language: Find the average order size for every customer who has made at least one order, but only include customers with an average size above 5.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_order_size FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING AVG(oi.quantity) > 5

natural_language: Retrieve the names of customers who live in the 'central' region and have placed completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List the number of orders and total amount for customers in the corporate segment who ordered more than 3 items.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 3

natural_language: Get the count of orders and the total sales for each product category, but only include categories that have generated over $1000 in total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Determine the total sales amount for each product category in orders marked as cancelled, only including categories with total sales above $5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Identify customer segments that have a greater than average spending and return the average spending by those segments.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders)

natural_language: Fetch the details of customers who have never placed an order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Retrieve all order items for a specific order ID of 123.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 123;

natural_language: Find the employees who have the highest total sales through orders they processed, and also provide the average total amount of those orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Identify the total number of products sold grouped by category for completed orders, excluding categories with less than 10 products sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) >= 10

natural_language: Find products that have a price between $10 and $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 10 AND 30;

natural_language: Find all completed orders with a total amount of exactly $150.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount = 150;

natural_language: Identify the top 3 products sold in the east region and their total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: List the customer segments that have made orders totaling over $50,000.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 50000;

natural_language: List all customers in the corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get customers that signed up in December 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) = 12 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2022;

natural_language: Show distinct customer segments for customers who have made more than 5 orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5;

natural_language: Retrieve a list of all orders along with the corresponding customer name, employee name, and the total number of products in that order, only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name AS customer_name, e.full_name AS employee_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_products FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id, c.full_name, e.full_name

natural_language: Retrieve all orders that were cancelled in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Determine the total number of unique products sold in completed orders by each employee.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Fetch the names of customers who reside in 'New York' and have made at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Retrieve all employees with a commission rate less than or equal to 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate <= 0.05;

natural_language: Find the products that were ordered in more than 10 different orders and list their total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) > 10

natural_language: Retrieve all orders and their total amounts for customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Show all customers who have a full name containing 'Smith'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE full_name LIKE '%Smith%';

natural_language: Get all customers who are in the retail segment and signed up in 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail' AND signup_date >= '2021-01-01' AND signup_date < '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Get the number of orders and average total amount per order for each city, filtering out cities with fewer than 10 total orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 10

natural_language: Show all products with a sales count of more than 500, displaying product name and category.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Find the two employees with the highest total sales attributed to their orders, and return their names and total sales.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 2;

natural_language: Identify employees who have sold the highest value of products in the 'Home Appliances' category, including their commission based on their sales.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Home Appliances' GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY total_commission DESC;

natural_language: List employees and the total amount of completed orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_processed FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Identify which products have been sold in more than five different orders along with their corresponding total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Find which products have not been sold at all.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.order_item_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Find the product names and their categories for products that have been ordered at least once.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name, p.category FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the full name and signup date of customers who have placed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name, customers.signup_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id;

natural_language: List all employees along with their commission rates who handle orders with a total amount greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Find customers in the city of Los Angeles.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM customers WHERE city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Identify the distinct customers who have made orders that include items from more than three different categories.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3;

natural_language: Find the top 5 products that generate the highest revenue from completed orders, showing their names and total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Show the total quantity of products sold by category, but only for categories that have sold more than 50 items.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Retrieve the total quantity sold by region, but only include regions that generated more than $5000 in revenue from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.region HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 5000

natural_language: Retrieve product names and the total quantity sold for each product.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: Count the number of cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_cancelled_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Retrieve the details of the most expensive product sold in orders placed by corporate customers, along with the total sales number.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, MAX(p.price) AS max_price, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY max_price DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Identify employees who have achieved a total sales amount of over $50,000 by product category.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, p.category HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 50000

natural_language: Find all employees and their corresponding commission rates based on the orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id;

natural_language: Determine the total number of products sold and total revenue generated for completed orders in the central region, categorized by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Find products that have a total sold quantity greater than 100 and their average selling price, filtering for categories that have total revenue exceeding 10000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100 AND SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000

natural_language: Retrieve the full names and email addresses of all customers who have placed an order, along with the total amount of those orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the customers who have made the highest total spending on products categorized as 'electronics', including their names and total spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.full_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

natural_language: Find the total number of items sold for each product.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_sold FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: Find the number of unique customers who have purchased products in the 'furniture' category and their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS unique_customers, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_spent FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE p.category = 'furniture' GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and total amount spent by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: List all completed orders from the month of January 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

natural_language: Retrieve the employees and the number of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Find products that have been ordered with a price higher than their cost.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id WHERE order_items.unit_price > products.cost;

natural_language: List corporate customers who have made at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: List products that have been sold in completed orders, categorizing them based on the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC;

natural_language: Retrieve all products with a cost of exactly $15.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost = 15;

natural_language: Retrieve the full names and total commissions of employees based on their processed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commissions FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated by each employee and their region, including employees who have not processed any orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amount), 0) AS total_revenue FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.region;

natural_language: Identify the products that are frequently bought together based on order items, and list the product pairs along with the count of their co-occurrences.
sql_query: SELECT oi1.product_id AS product1, oi2.product_id AS product2, COUNT(*) AS co_occurrence_count FROM order_items oi1 INNER JOIN order_items oi2 ON oi1.order_id = oi2.order_id AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id GROUP BY oi1.product_id, oi2.product_id ORDER BY co_occurrence_count DESC;

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered by corporate customers, along with the total number of times each product was ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS times_ordered FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List all products along with their categories and the total amount of orders they are linked to.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, products.category, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_orders FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name, products.category;

natural_language: Get the regions where employees work and the count of orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.region, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.region;

natural_language: Get the names of all retail customers who have placed an order and the order status.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: List customers who placed orders for products from the 'electronics' category and whose total spending exceeds $8,000.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 8000

natural_language: List customers and the count of their orders, including only those with order totals greater than $100.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.total_amount > 100 GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: List the total number of orders and their statuses for each customer.
