sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count, orders.status FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name, orders.status;

natural_language: Count the number of employees in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE region = 'central';

natural_language: Find the average order value for each customer segment, considering completed and cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List all orders that were made on or before December 31, 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date <= '2022-12-31';

natural_language: Find the total number of orders placed by customers from the city 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(orders.order_id) FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'New York';

natural_language: List all employees along with their commission rates and the status of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, o.status FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id;

natural_language: Find the average order total for corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Find the total sales for each product where total sales are higher than 2000 and the product has been sold in at least five orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000 AND COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) >= 5

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated for each category of products sold to customers in the 'retail' segment, along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the total revenue from orders in the central region and the respective order statuses.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount), o.status FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: Find the best-selling product in the west region along with its total quantity sold and total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) as total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Find products that were ordered more than 20 times in total, grouped by category and showing the total quantity sold in each category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Get a list of products that are out of stock (assuming cost = 0).
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost = 0;

natural_language: List the segments of customers whose total spending exceeds $50,000, including the total spending for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 50000

natural_language: Find the total amount of sales for each product, including the average price, and only include products with more than 10 units sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Get all orders that were placed in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: List the top 3 products by total sales amount and the number of unique customers who bought them.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: List the email addresses and order dates for customers who have pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email, orders.order_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: List the total sales per product category for orders placed by VIP customers only.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the names of employees who are associated with completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the average price of products sold by each employee along with the count of products sold.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(oi.product_id) AS products_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Get products priced between $50 and $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 50 AND 200;

natural_language: Determine the total number of orders placed in each segment and the average order total for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders with a total amount equal to $500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount = 500;

natural_language: Identify the customers who have made more than five orders and find their total spending, grouped by segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Find customers who have a full name starting with 'J'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE full_name LIKE 'J%';

natural_language: List employees from the 'west' region and their respective order totals.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'west' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total sales per product category for completed orders from retail customers, and show only categories with total sales over $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders AS o INNER JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id INNER JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 500

natural_language: Get the breakdown of order statuses for each customer, showing how many orders they made in total and the status of each order (completed or cancelled).
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, o.status

natural_language: Get the total order amount and the average product price for customers in the retail segment who have placed more than three orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount, AVG(p.price) AS average_product_price FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 3

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold by each product category for completed orders within the last month.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List the number of orders and total sales for each product category for completed orders, only include categories with total sales over 1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Find all retail customers and the total amounts of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: List the segments of customers and the total number of unique products they have ordered.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_ordered FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the average number of items per order for completed orders segmented by customer city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_items_per_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Get the total number of items sold and the total revenue generated for each product, including only products sold to corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name;

natural_language: Calculate the total quantity sold and the average price for products in the 'toys' category during the current year.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'toys' AND o.order_date >= DATE_TRUNC('year', CURRENT_DATE);

natural_language: Find customers from the 'corporate' segment along with the total number of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: List all employees and the number of completed orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find all orders placed on '2023-10-01'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-10-01';

natural_language: List all products that have been sold in cancelled orders, along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name;

natural_language: Find the average order total for each employee in the east region, but only include orders that have at least two order items.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' AND o.order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id HAVING COUNT(order_item_id) >= 2) GROUP BY e.full_name

natural_language: Find all employees working in the central region and the orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, o.order_id FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central';

natural_language: Identify the products with the highest quantity sold, along with the total revenue for those products, and filter to those generating over $2000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 2000

natural_language: Show the count of unique customers for each product based on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_buyers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: Find the customer segments that have an average order total greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 500;

natural_language: Find all orders with a status of cancelled that were placed in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: Retrieve each product's total revenue and total quantity sold, excluding products with no sales, sorted by total revenue in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p LEFT JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 0 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

natural_language: Show all products with a price of $20 or less.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price <= 20;

natural_language: List all corporate customers who signed up in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND signup_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31';

natural_language: Find the sales performance of each product category by calculating the total revenue and the number of unique customers who purchased from each category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) as total_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) as unique_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the total revenue generated from orders in the 'east' region for each product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Show the total amounts of pending orders grouped by product categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_pending_amount FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Show the total sales amount for each customer based on their completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated by each product category, showing only categories with total revenue greater than $3000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 3000

natural_language: Get the list of products that have been ordered by customers in the 'vip' segment and their total sales volume.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_volume FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have a price between $20 and $80.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 20 AND 80;

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of cancelled orders along with the employee names who handled them.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS cancelled_orders FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Show all order items with a unit price less than $5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price < 5;

natural_language: List all products sold in orders that have a status of 'completed', along with the total sales and total quantity sold, excluding those products that have total sales under $1,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Get the average order amount for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, AVG(orders.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Find the total number of orders along with the city of the customers who placed them.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, c.city FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders placed on July 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-07-01';

natural_language: List all products ordered along with their categories and the total quantity ordered.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, products.category, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_id;

natural_language: List the total number of orders made by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) as total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get all order items that have a unit price of exactly $10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price = 10;

natural_language: Find the total revenue from completed orders grouped by employee.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve a summary of total sales and distinct customers for each product, only considering sales from VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name

natural_language: Retrieve all orders with a total amount less than or equal to $250.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount <= 250;

natural_language: Identify customers who have a total spending exceeding the average spending of all customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_spending) FROM (SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total_spending FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) AS avg_spending);

natural_language: List all employees with an employee ID greater than 100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE employee_id > 100;

natural_language: List all products that were ordered by VIP customers, along with the total quantity sold and the total revenue generated from those orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id

natural_language: Find the most common product purchased by the 'corporate' segment customers, along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: List all customers who signed up after June 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2023-06-30';

natural_language: Show all completed orders from the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 day';

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in the central region by employees, including only those products sold through completed orders.
sql_query:
SELECT AVG(p.price) AS avg_product_price
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id
WHERE e.region = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Show all customers who signed up in March 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2021-03-01' AND '2021-03-31';

natural_language: Retrieve the average order value for each employee along with the number of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name

natural_language: List the total number of orders and the total revenue generated from each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Determine the average cost of goods sold for products in completed orders by segment of the customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(p.cost) AS average_cost_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the count of orders and total amount spent for VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Retrieve all products that are priced at exactly $49.99.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 49.99;

natural_language: Determine the total number of orders and average total amount for products in the 'electronics' category for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_total_amount FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'electronics';

natural_language: Get the average total spend of customers for each segment, considering only those who have made at least 3 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(total_spent) AS average_spend FROM (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) >= 3) AS subquery JOIN customers AS c ON subquery.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Show all customers who signed up in the last 30 days.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 day';

natural_language: Get a list of all customers along with the number of completed orders they have made and the total amount spent.
sql_query:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name;

natural_language: Show all customers that signed up before January 1, 2019.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2019-01-01';

natural_language: Identify employees who have processed orders exceeding $5000 in total for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY e.full_name, c.segment HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 5000

natural_language: Determine which products have not been sold and include their cost and profit margin.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.cost, (p.price - p.cost) AS profit_margin FROM products p WHERE p.product_id NOT IN (SELECT oi.product_id FROM order_items oi);

natural_language: Find the average order total for each product category sold by employees in the 'east' region.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the names of employees and the number of orders they have handled.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS orders_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get the number of orders grouped by each status type and the total revenue generated for each status.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders o GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: Get the total sales for each product in completed orders, only for products with sales greater than $200.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 200

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated by orders in the 'pending' status for each product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List all employees along with their total sales and the number of orders they processed, including only those employees who have processed more than 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 10

natural_language: Find customers who have made more than three orders and list their names along with the total spent on those orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 3

natural_language: List the segments of customers who have placed orders totaling more than $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.segment FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: List the customer details who have made multiple orders totaling over $10,000, including their signup date and segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, c.city, c.signup_date, c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Retrieve the most recent order date for each customer, along with their full name and total amount spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS most_recent_order_date, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total costs of products sold per product for those that have generated revenue over $5,000, calculating the total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Fetch the statuses of orders along with the employee names who processed them.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, e.full_name FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id;

natural_language: Determine the total sales for each product category by employee region, only including orders placed in the last year.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' GROUP BY p.category, e.region;

natural_language: Get the average price of products sold in orders that were placed by corporate segment customers, including only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Show the employee names and the count of orders they have completed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Select all orders placed on '2023-05-15'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-05-15';

natural_language: Show all employees who have a commission rate of exactly 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate = 0.05;

natural_language: Retrieve the total expenditure on products by each segment type in the last year, and display those segments where total expenditure exceeds $10,000.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_expenditure FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 YEAR' GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 10000

natural_language: Get the total spending of customers who belong to the corporate segment.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Get a list of employees along with the total sales they generated from 'clothing' products, only displaying those whose total sales exceed $5,000.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'clothing' GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Find the customer who has spent the most in total amount and display their full name, city, and signup date.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.city, c.signup_date, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.city, c.signup_date ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Get the average price of products sold by each employee, only including those with a completed order.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_product_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name;

natural_language: Get the average total amount for orders made by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(orders.total_amount) AS average_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: List the top five segments by average total amount spent per order, including the segment name.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY avg_spent DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List all products priced above $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > 20;

natural_language: Find all employees from the central region with a commission rate of 15%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'central' AND commission_rate = 0.15;

natural_language: Get a list of all product categories along with their corresponding total sales amount, but only for categories where total sales exceed $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated by each product, but only for products that have been ordered and for orders completed.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of all pending orders along with the names of the customers who placed them.
sql_query: SELECT o.total_amount, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get the names of employees along with the total number of orders they've processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the segments of customers who have ordered products priced above $100, along with the count of those customers in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.price > 100 GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get a report of the breakdown of total spending by each customer segment with percentages that each segment contributes to the overall revenue.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, (SUM(o.total_amount) / (SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM orders)) * 100 AS percentage_of_total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Get customers who signed up in the last week.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 day';

natural_language: Find all products that have been ordered along with the total quantities sold in each order.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get a summary of the total number of products sold by category.
sql_query: SELECT products.category, SUM(order_items.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id GROUP BY products.category;

natural_language: Retrieve the top 3 regions by total sales amount and the corresponding average order amount for those regions.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated from corporate customers' orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Retrieve the average price of products sold in each category, including only those categories with an average price above 50.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS avg_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(p.price) > 50

natural_language: Find all corporate customers who signed up before 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND signup_date < '2021-01-01';

natural_language: Find all order items associated with a specific product ID, say 101.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE product_id = 101;

natural_language: Retrieve the average cost of products sold in completed orders along with the total count of those products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, AVG(p.cost) AS avg_cost, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name;

natural_language: List all customers from the city of Paris who are in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Paris' AND segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Get all products that have a price greater than or equal to $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price >= 30;

natural_language: Get a list of all products that have been sold with an average price higher than their average cost, along with their respective profit margins.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_selling_price, AVG(p.cost) AS avg_cost, (AVG(oi.unit_price) - AVG(p.cost)) AS profit_margin FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING AVG(oi.unit_price) > AVG(p.cost)

natural_language: Identify which product categories have more than 10 unique products sold in orders, and calculate the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) > 10

natural_language: Retrieve the names of all products ordered more than 10 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10;

natural_language: Get the monthly revenue for each product category for the past year.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) AS month, SUM(o.total_amount) AS monthly_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' GROUP BY p.category, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date);

natural_language: Determine the top 3 products with the highest total sales amount and the number of orders they were included in, only considering completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Show all cancelled orders from March 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND order_date BETWEEN '2023-03-01' AND '2023-03-31';

natural_language: Retrieve the full names of customers who have completed at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the most popular product (by total quantity sold) and the total revenue generated from that product, for customers that are in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Find the total sales amount for each product ordered by 'corporate' segment customers, only if the total sales exceed $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Find the total amount spent by customers from the city 'New York' on their orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Select the total amount spent by corporate customers from the east region, grouping the results by customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND e.region = 'east' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Identify cities with average product prices over $100 where at least 10 different products are sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS avg_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(p.price) > 100 AND COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) >= 10

natural_language: List all completed orders with a total amount below $500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount < 500;

natural_language: Retrieve the names of customers who have ordered products from more than 3 different categories, along with the number of distinct categories they have ordered from.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of completed and cancelled orders for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(CASE WHEN orders.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN orders.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Show all products in the 'clothing' category with a price under $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'clothing' AND price < 30;

natural_language: Get the full names and emails of customers who have placed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Find all customers who are part of the corporate segment and live in 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Find the employee with the highest total sales and their commission earned based on a rigid threshold of $1000.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000 ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Get the total amount of all pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total_pending FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get customer names along with the number of unique products they purchased in total, filtering for customers with more than 5 unique products.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 5

natural_language: Get all customers in the 'corporate' segment who signed up this year.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2023;

natural_language: Retrieve the average order total for each customer segment, along with the total number of orders for each segment, sorted by the average order total in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY average_order_total DESC

natural_language: Get all orders associated with a specific customer using their ID.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 123;

natural_language: Calculate the total order value for each product category, including only products with sales greater than $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Count the total products available in the inventory.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products;

natural_language: Show all order items for orders over $500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price * quantity > 500;

natural_language: Find all products that are currently priced at $10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 10;

natural_language: Get the average total amount of completed orders made by each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List the top 5 products based on total quantity sold across all orders, including the product name and the total quantity, only including products that have been sold more than 100 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100 ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Get a list of all employees in the east region with a commission rate of 15% or more.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'east' AND commission_rate >= 0.15;

natural_language: Find the employees who have sold products in the 'electronics' category with an average sale price greater than $100.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_price FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name HAVING AVG(oi.unit_price) > 100

natural_language: List all customers living in New York or Chicago.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city IN ('New York', 'Chicago');

natural_language: Find the number of unique products sold per segment type of customers, including segment names.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_sold FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the average order amount and total orders for each customer type who have placed more than three orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 3

natural_language: Calculate the total revenue generated for each product in the corporate segment, grouping results by product and including the average price.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who signed up within the last 30 days and their first order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.signup_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 days' LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List the full names and email addresses of customers who have completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the customer segments that have the highest average order amount, along with the count of orders for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY avg_order_amount DESC;

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have a cost higher than $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > 30;

natural_language: Get the total amount spent by each customer who has made more than five orders, along with the number of orders they made.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Retrieve the top 3 products sold by quantity along with their total revenue, for each employee, who completed more than 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name AS employee_name, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id, p.product_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 10 ORDER BY e.full_name, total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3

natural_language: Retrieve the list of products that have been sold in orders with a total amount greater than $1000, grouped by product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.total_amount > 1000 GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get the total sales by region and the average number of orders per employee in that region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT e.employee_id) AS avg_orders_per_employee FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Find the employee IDs and names of employees who have not completed any orders, along with the count of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) = 0;

natural_language: Identify the most profitable product based on the sum of the difference between total sales and costs.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM((oi.unit_price - p.cost) * oi.quantity) as profit FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY profit DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders with a total amount less than or equal to $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount <= 20;

natural_language: Find the names of customers who have ordered products with a total cost greater than $500 and include their signup date.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE (oi.quantity * p.cost) > 500;

natural_language: Find the average order value for each employee, but only include those who have processed more than 5 orders in total, and sort them by average order value descending.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5 ORDER BY average_order_value DESC

natural_language: Find the number of orders placed by each employee.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: List all customers who have placed at least one order with a total amount greater than the average total amount of all orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.total_amount > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders);

natural_language: Get the list of employees and the number of pending orders assigned to them.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS pending_orders FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get a count of customers in each city who have made pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, COUNT(customers.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: Identify products that only VIP customers have purchased, along with the total number of these products sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip')

natural_language: Get the total amount of orders placed by each corporate customer.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve employee names and their commission rates.
sql_query: SELECT full_name, commission_rate FROM employees;

natural_language: Retrieve all order items for a specific order.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 1;

natural_language: Find all products with a cost greater than $75.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > 75;

natural_language: Find the cities that have both retail and corporate customers, along with the count of customers in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'retail' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS retail_count, SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'corporate' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS corporate_count FROM customers AS c GROUP BY c.city HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'retail' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'corporate' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0

natural_language: Get the most recent order date for each customer, along with the total number of products they purchased.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order_date, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_purchased FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id

natural_language: Get the list of customers who have orders in a pending status.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Show employee names and their regions who have processed orders totaling more than $1000.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT e.full_name, e.region FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Select all orders that total 250 or more.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount >= 250;

natural_language: Calculate the total amount of orders placed by each customer in their respective cities and their order counts.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city, c.full_name;

natural_language: Show all products with a price between $20 and $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 20 AND 200;

natural_language: Get the total quantity sold for each product that has a selling price above $50 and has been ordered at least 10 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.price > 50 AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) >= 10

natural_language: List employees who have processed orders in the last month along with the order count.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month' GROUP BY employees.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of orders and total spending for each city, including the city name, ordered by total spending in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city ORDER BY total_spending DESC;

natural_language: Find the total amount of orders for each customer along with their full name.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders completed on '2022-03-15'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date = '2022-03-15';

natural_language: List all orders with a total amount less than or equal to $500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount <= 500;

natural_language: List products with a price exactly equal to $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 200;

natural_language: List all products that belong to the 'electronics' category.
sql_query: SELECT product_name FROM products WHERE category = 'electronics';

natural_language: Get a list of all products sold, with their total sales volume and revenue, filtering for products where the revenue generated is greater than $5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sales_volume, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS revenue_generated FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 5000

natural_language: Get the average total amount of orders for each product category, filtering for categories with an average over $100.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 100

natural_language: List the employees who have the highest sales totals, along with their respective regions, limited to the top 10 employees.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.region ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 10;

natural_language: Find the order count for employees in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the average commission rate of all employees.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(commission_rate) AS average_commission FROM employees;

natural_language: Identify the customers who have purchased products from at least two different categories, including their full name and the number of distinct categories they have purchased from.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) >= 2

natural_language: Determine the most frequently sold product across all orders, aggregated by the quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Find the most popular product category based on the number of orders it appears in, counting only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Find all employees who have processed orders totaling more than $50,000, along with their commission earned from these orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM orders AS o JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 50000

natural_language: Get all customers who signed up before January 1, 2020.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2020-01-01';

natural_language: Get the full names of all customers who signed up after January 1, 2022.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Get the product details for products that have been ordered more than 10 times and have a price exceeding $50, along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category, p.price, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10 AND p.price > 50

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who live in Chicago and signed up in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chicago' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2023;

natural_language: Get a list of all employees in the 'west' region.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM employees WHERE region = 'west';

natural_language: Get all customers in California who are VIP.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'California' AND segment = 'vip';

natural_language: List the full names of customers along with their order dates for all completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve all products with a price equal to $99.99.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 99.99;

natural_language: List the total amount for completed orders along with the names of customers who made those orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the number of completed orders and the total revenue for each product category sold to retail customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the list of products and their total sales amount attributed to corporate customers, filtered to show only those with sales exceeding $1,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Get the total count of products sold in 'Furniture' category along with their names.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Furniture' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Find the average order total for corporate customers served by employees from the east region.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND e.region = 'east';

natural_language: Count the number of products in the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture';

natural_language: List the customers who have made orders worth more than $500, including their email and city.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.email, c.city HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 500

natural_language: List all customers who have placed more than 5 orders and the total spent by each customer grouped by their city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: List all order items with their corresponding product names and prices.
sql_query: SELECT order_items.order_item_id, products.product_name, order_items.unit_price FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id;

natural_language: Get all orders where the total amount is exactly 75.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount = 75;

natural_language: Calculate the percentage of completed orders relative to total orders for each customer segment, showing the segment name and the percentage.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, (COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(o.order_id)) AS completed_percentage FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the total number of orders and the average order value by category of products.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the total amount of orders grouped by employee region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Get total amount and status of orders made by customers living in 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT o.total_amount, o.status FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Get the most recent order date for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve products that are neither in the electronics nor the furniture category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category NOT IN ('electronics', 'furniture');

natural_language: Get a list of products that have been sold at least 15 times, along with their total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) >= 15

natural_language: List all customers who have made purchases over $500 along with their total spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 500

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of orders and the corresponding total amount for each employee, only considering orders with the status 'completed' and products sold in the 'electronics' category.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY e.employee_id

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered, along with the total amount for each order.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_id, products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price) AS total_ordered FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the names of employees who have completed orders that total over $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' AND orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Find the average number of items per order and total sales amount for each order status.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_items_per_order, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales_amount FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of products sold and total revenue generated for completed orders by segment and region.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, e.region, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment, e.region;

natural_language: Get the details of employees who have processed orders with a total amount above $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name, orders.total_amount FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Find all orders placed on or after December 1st, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2023-12-01';

natural_language: Find all products that have a price between $30 and $70.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 30 AND 70;

natural_language: Fetch all orders that have been cancelled along with the corresponding customer names and order dates.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.full_name, orders.order_date FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Find the customer with the maximum total amount spent who has ordered products from both 'books' and 'electronics', along with their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.customer_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category IN ('books', 'electronics') GROUP BY o.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = 2) GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Find the average commission rate of employees in the 'west' region.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(commission_rate) FROM employees WHERE region = 'west';

natural_language: Get all completed orders that have a total amount between $50 and $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount BETWEEN 50 AND 100;

natural_language: Identify which customers have never placed a cancelled order, along with the total amount they have spent on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0

natural_language: Find the total number of distinct products sold in each category from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) as distinct_products FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the order details, including customer names and order status, for orders made by retail customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_id, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Find all orders that have a total amount greater than $100 and the corresponding customer details.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.full_name, customers.email FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 100;

natural_language: Identify employees who have a commission rate greater than the average commission rate and list their names, regions, and total sales they generated from completed orders in the last fiscal year.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.commission_rate > (SELECT AVG(commission_rate) FROM employees) AND o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date >= '2022-10-01' AND o.order_date < '2023-10-01' GROUP BY e.employee_id

natural_language: Retrieve the count of distinct products sold per category by each employee, considering only orders with a pending status.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_products_count FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY e.full_name, p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 5

natural_language: Summarize total sales by product category for the last quarter's completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 month' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Show all products that have a price less than or equal to $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price <= 50;

natural_language: Count the number of orders for each status type.
sql_query: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY status;

natural_language: Show all order items where the unit price is $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price = 20;

natural_language: List all employees and the total number of orders they have processed.
