sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: List the categories and the total revenue generated from each category for all orders made by VIP customers in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date) = 2023 GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Get all orders placed on '2023-08-15'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-08-15';

natural_language: Determine the total distinct products sold by retail customers where total sales exceed $5,000.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS total_products_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.customer_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Show the total quantity and total sales for each product in the 'Electronics' category where total sales exceed $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Find products with a price greater than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > 50;

natural_language: Show all employees who have a commission rate of at least 5%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate >= 0.05;

natural_language: Find the total sales made by each employee for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve a list of all customers who live in the 'central' region and the dates they signed up.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'central';

natural_language: Show the total sales amount per employee for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders for a specific employee ID 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE employee_id = 5;

natural_language: Retrieve products with a name that contains 'wireless'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%wireless%';

natural_language: Get the average order total for customers in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) as average_order_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Show the order IDs along with the customer email for orders that are pending.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.email FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Retrieve the names and cities of customers who have canceled their orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Find the highest selling product in each category and the total revenue it generated.
sql_query: WITH RankedProducts AS ( SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.category ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) DESC) AS rank FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category, p.product_name ) SELECT category, product_name, total_revenue FROM RankedProducts WHERE rank = 1;

natural_language: Find the total price of products ordered and the corresponding order date.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(order_items.unit_price * order_items.quantity) AS total_price, orders.order_date FROM order_items JOIN orders ON order_items.order_id = orders.order_id GROUP BY orders.order_date;

natural_language: List all products in the home appliances category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'home appliances';

natural_language: List all customers whose full names start with the letter 'A'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE full_name LIKE 'A%';

natural_language: Get total orders per employee for completed orders only.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Identify product categories with sales lower than the average sales across all categories in completed orders, including the total sales for each low-performing category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) < (SELECT AVG(category_sales) FROM (SELECT SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS category_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category) AS avg_sales)

natural_language: List the top 5 employees based on the total sales amount they generated from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered more than 100 times, along with their average selling price and total revenue generated from those orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_orders, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_price, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 100

natural_language: Get the total amount of orders grouped by each employee's name.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total count of orders and total revenue generated from orders made by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Find all customers from the city 'Chicago' who are in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chicago' AND segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get the top 5 products by total sales amount, including their category, where the total sales exceed $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000 ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Identify which customer segment prefers which product category based on their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment, p.category;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders along with the associated customer's city.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, customers.city FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Fetch the names of customers who live in a specific city along with their order statuses.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.status FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold and the corresponding revenue for products belonging to the same category, where total sales exceed $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Retrieve a list of customers and the total number of orders they've placed, regardless of status.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of completed orders for customers segmented as 'vip'.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_completed FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List the total number of items sold per product category for completed orders, only including categories with more than 10 items sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: List all products with their prices.
sql_query: SELECT product_name, price FROM products;

natural_language: Get the total amount of cancelled orders categorized by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_cancelled_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Generate a report of products sold that have a higher profit margin than the average profit margin of all products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, (p.price - p.cost) AS profit_margin FROM products p WHERE (p.price - p.cost) > (SELECT AVG(price - cost) FROM products)

natural_language: Retrieve product categories that have generated total sales over $10000 in completed orders for 'corporate' segment customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 10000

natural_language: Find the number of orders placed by each customer and their average order value, filtering out customers with fewer than 3 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3

natural_language: Retrieve the city and email of customers who have placed a pending order.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Calculate the average price of products sold in each category, but only include categories with sales exceeding $2000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS avg_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: Retrieve orders with status 'cancelled' and total amount less than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND total_amount < 50;

natural_language: Get the count of pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS pending_orders_count FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';

natural_language: List all products that were ordered with a total quantity greater than 10 and show the total revenue generated for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Find the names of employees and the number of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS number_of_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find products that have generated more than $3000 in total sales and list their categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 3000

natural_language: List all orders made on March 15, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-03-15';

natural_language: Find the most popular product category based on the number of times products were sold by region.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, e.region, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY p.category, e.region ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get the list of customers who are in the 'vip' segment and have made a purchase.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Find the total number of different products ordered by each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_products_ordered FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List the total number of products ordered and the total amount for each order.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, COUNT(order_items.product_id) AS total_products, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN order_items ON orders.order_id = order_items.order_id GROUP BY orders.order_id;

natural_language: Calculate the total count of products sold to retail customers, grouped by product name, with the product cost included.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, p.cost FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_name, p.cost;

natural_language: List the cities and their corresponding total order amounts, only for those cities where the average total amount of orders exceeds $300.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 300

natural_language: List customer full names and their corresponding order dates for any pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: List all employees and their total sales amount from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Identify the most popular product category in terms of total sales and the corresponding total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Identify which products have been ordered by corporate customers, including the total quantity ordered, but only show products that have been ordered more than 50 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Fetch the total number of orders and average order total for each product category, only include categories where total orders exceed 20.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_total FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 20

natural_language: Get the average product price for all products that have been sold.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount spent by corporate segment customers grouped by employee, filtering to show only those employees who managed corporate customers that spent over $5000.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 5000

natural_language: List the regions of employees who have processed orders with a total amount greater than 1000.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT e.region FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Get the full names of employees working in the 'east' region.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM employees WHERE region = 'east';

natural_language: Get a count of all products in the 'electronics' category.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = 'electronics';

natural_language: List the order IDs along with the names of the customers who have placed them.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

natural_language: List employees along with the regions they operate in and the orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, o.order_id FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id;

natural_language: Identify the top five products by total revenue, including only products that have been sold more than 50 times.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered by VIP customers, along with the total quantity ordered for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Determine the total revenue and average quantity per order item for products in the 'electronics' category.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics';

natural_language: Count the number of orders in each status for each product category, showing categories with more than 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, o.status, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category, o.status HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 10

natural_language: Calculate the total quantity of products sold for each product name, considering only completed orders, and filter out products with less than 10 sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) >= 10

natural_language: Determine the average order value for each customer segment and the highest total spent by a customer in that segment.
sql_query:
SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_value, MAX(o.total_amount) AS highest_order
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the total sales for each region, showing only regions that have at least two employees and excluding cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders AS o JOIN employees AS e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND e.region IN (SELECT region FROM employees GROUP BY region HAVING COUNT(employee_id) >= 2) GROUP BY e.region

natural_language: Get all orders placed in the month of September 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 9 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: List all customers who have placed orders with more than 3 different products, with their names and the count of distinct products.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_product_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 3

natural_language: Get all customers who have their signup date in the last year.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 year';

natural_language: Show all orders made by customers from Chicago.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chicago');

natural_language: Find the total number of unique products sold to each segment with their total revenue from those sales.
sql_query:
SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS unique_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the names and commission rates of employees who work in the east region and have completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'east' AND orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the average total amount of orders placed by customers from New York.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Find the average number of items ordered per order for customers in the 'vip' segment, only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(item_count) AS average_items FROM (SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS item_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id) AS order_summary;

natural_language: Get the product names and total order quantities for products that have more than 10 units sold in total, filtered by completed orders only.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Identify the top three most profitable products, based on total profit from orders, in each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * (oi.unit_price - p.cost)) AS total_profit FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment, p.product_name ORDER BY total_profit DESC

natural_language: List all the employees who have processed orders in the 'completed' status along with their commission rates.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the list of products that have been sold by more than one employee within completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT e.employee_id) > 1;

natural_language: List all products with a cost less than $15.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost < 15;

natural_language: Show all customers who have made any orders.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders);

natural_language: Get the count of orders and total amount for orders placed by retail customers.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Retrieve the emails of customers and the total amounts of their orders during signup.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.signup_date <= orders.order_date GROUP BY customers.email;

natural_language: Find all employees who have processed orders in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'east';

natural_language: Retrieve the names and prices of products that have been ordered, along with their corresponding order IDs.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, products.price, order_items.order_id FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id;

natural_language: Get the average order total for corporate customers by region of the employee who handled the order.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Find the customer segment that has the highest ratio of completed to cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_orders, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders, (COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) / COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END)) AS completed_to_cancelled_ratio FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY completed_to_cancelled_ratio DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get a list of product categories that generated revenue greater than $5000 and the total revenue from those categories for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 5000

natural_language: Find all VIP customers who signed up after January 1, 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip' AND signup_date > '2022-01-01';

natural_language: Get the average quantity of products sold per order for each category, but only include categories with average quantities above 5.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(oi.quantity) > 5

natural_language: Gather the total amount of sales for each product category sold by employees from the 'central' region, in descending order.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_sales DESC;

natural_language: Identify the products that have generated the most revenue in the 'electronics' category and the total revenue for those products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

natural_language: Get the list of products that have been ordered but have a price lower than their cost.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id WHERE oi.unit_price < p.cost;

natural_language: Identify customers who have ordered products from more than 3 different categories.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3;

natural_language: Retrieve the average price of products ordered by VIP customers and the number of distinct products they ordered.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_price, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS distinct_products FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip'

natural_language: Get all customers from the city of London.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'London';

natural_language: Get all products with the name 'Laptop'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name = 'Laptop';

natural_language: Find all products along with their price that have been ordered.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT products.product_name, products.price FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id;

natural_language: Retrieve completed orders along with the quantity of each item ordered.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, order_items.quantity FROM orders JOIN order_items ON orders.order_id = order_items.order_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Show all orders placed after March 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date > '2023-03-01';

natural_language: Find customers who have ordered products from more than 3 different categories, along with their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: List the product categories that have generated more than $1000 in total sales, and their corresponding total sales amounts.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: List all product categories along with the total count of distinct products in each category, but only include categories that have an average price above 50.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS product_count FROM products AS p GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(p.price) > 50

natural_language: List the customers who have made purchases from more than three different product categories and the total amount they spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Show all orders with a total amount of at least $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount >= 100;

natural_language: List order details for all orders placed in the last week.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 days';

natural_language: Show the total number of orders placed by customers in 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Calculate the total sales amount by category of products for orders that have been cancelled, along with the category names.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Count the number of distinct products ordered by each customer and return the results only for customers who have made more than 5 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_products FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Get the total amount of completed orders along with the names of the customers.
sql_query: SELECT orders.total_amount, customers.full_name FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List the names of products along with the total number of times they have been ordered and total revenue, only for those with total revenue over $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Find all orders where the total amount is between 200 and 300.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount BETWEEN 200 AND 300;

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold for each completed order.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY o.order_id;

natural_language: Find the total number of products ordered along with the order ID.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who are in the VIP segment and live in 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip' AND city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Retrieve total sales amount for each category of products.
sql_query: SELECT products.category, SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.category;

natural_language: Find all products in the 'Clothing' category with a price greater than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Clothing' AND price > 50;

natural_language: Get all customers who signed up before 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2021-01-01';

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered and calculate the total revenue generated from each product, showing only those with revenue above $5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Find the most recent order date for each product along with the associated customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date, c.segment FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.product_id, c.segment;

natural_language: Get the total expenses for each order by multiplying quantity by unit price, showing order id and total expense.
sql_query: SELECT oi.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_expense FROM order_items oi GROUP BY oi.order_id;

natural_language: Get all order items with a unit price that exceeds $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE unit_price > 30;

natural_language: Get the list of employees and the number of pending orders they have.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS pending_orders_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the average order amount for each customer segment, along with the total number of orders for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get the number of distinct customers who have made purchases in each product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find all products that cost less than their selling price.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost < price;

natural_language: Get the total quantity of products sold per region, filtering out regions where total sales quantity is less than 100.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.region HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) >= 100

natural_language: List the total number of orders and average order value for each customer segment where the average order value exceeds $100.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 100

natural_language: Retrieve the number of unique products purchased by each customer along with their total spent amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Get the total cost of all orders completed by employees in the 'central' region.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_completed FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get all employees with full names that end with 'son'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name LIKE '%son';

natural_language: Calculate the total number of products sold and total sales amount for each customer, filtering customers who have made more than 5 purchases.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Find all products with a price less than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price < 50;

natural_language: Get all products that cost less than $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost < 30;

natural_language: Find the commission rates of employees along with the total amounts from their respective orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.commission_rate;

natural_language: Retrieve the total count of cancelled orders by city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS cancelled_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: List all products that were never ordered by customers in the retail segment, along with their categories and prices.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, p.price FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' OR c.customer_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Retrieve a list of customers who have placed orders for products in the highest revenue category, along with the total revenue they generated.
sql_query: WITH highest_category AS (SELECT category FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY SUM(price) DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category IN (SELECT category FROM highest_category) GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders placed by customers living in the west region.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'west';

natural_language: List employees with their respective regions and count of completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, employees.region, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS completed_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name, employees.region;

natural_language: Get the average number of items per order for each customer in the VIP segment who has placed more than 5 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, AVG(oi.quantity) AS average_items_per_order FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Find the employee who has the highest average order amount from the orders they processed, including their region.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY average_order_amount DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List all products sold in orders placed by VIP customers, along with the total revenue generated from each product.
sql_query:
SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue 
FROM order_items oi 
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id 
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id 
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id 
WHERE c.segment = 'vip' 
GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Find all unique products sold in orders from customers in the corporate segment, counting only those products that have sold more than 20 units.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 20

natural_language: Find all orders placed in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: Find the average total amount of orders placed by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Show all customers who signed up before January 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date < '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Retrieve the signup dates for all customers with the VIP segment.
sql_query: SELECT signup_date FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Select all customers who signed up in the year 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date >= '2023-01-01';

natural_language: List all products sold in the last quarter, along with the total quantity sold and total revenue generated, for products that generated over $2000 in total revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 MONTH' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 2000

natural_language: Retrieve customers who have the highest average spending across their orders, and display their signup dates.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_spending, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY avg_spending DESC

natural_language: List all customers along with the order status of their last order.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.status FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.order_date = (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders WHERE orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id);

natural_language: Determine the average price of products sold by employees in the east region based on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND e.region = 'east' GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Determine the total sales and the total number of completed orders for each product category, while excluding categories with total sales below $1,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Find the customer who has the highest total spending on products from the 'electronics' category and return their full name, email, and the total amount spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List the product categories with their total sales amounts, but only include categories with total sales less than $5,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) < 5000

natural_language: Count the number of products in the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_furniture_products FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture';

natural_language: Calculate the total quantity of products sold by each segment of customers, filtering out segments that have less than 100 total products sold.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total sales revenue from completed orders, showing the revenue for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Show the total revenue generated by each employee from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) as total_revenue FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the total order amount and average quantity per order for each product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_amount, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity_per_order FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Generate a report of the average order value per customer segment, sorted by the highest average value.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY average_order_value DESC;

natural_language: Retrieve the employees who have the highest number of cancelled orders and the respective cancellation rate.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) as cancelled_orders, (COUNT(o.order_id) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) as cancellation_rate FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name ORDER BY cancelled_orders DESC;

natural_language: Get the average total amount of all completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the product that has the highest number of orders in the western region and its corresponding total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_orders DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve all pending orders with a total amount greater than 200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND total_amount > 200;

natural_language: List the customers who have products in their orders that are both above the average price and from the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND oi.unit_price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products);

natural_language: List employees along with the number of completed orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS completed_orders_count FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Get all orders placed in the month of March 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2023-03-01' AND order_date < '2023-04-01';

natural_language: Get the average spend per order for 'retail' customers, analyzed by each product category they ordered.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_spend_per_order FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Retrieve the total cost of products sold for each employee who processed completed orders in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: List all products and the average prices of sold quantities.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, AVG(order_items.unit_price) as average_price FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: Show the top three products sold in terms of revenue in each region, including the employee who made the highest sale of each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, e.region, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, e.full_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY p.product_name, e.region, e.full_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC

natural_language: Retrieve products that are part of the 'Furniture' category with a price between $50 and $500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture' AND price BETWEEN 50 AND 500;

natural_language: Find all products with names that contain 'widget'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%widget%';

natural_language: List the unique segments of customers who have made at least one order that include products from the electronics category.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics';

natural_language: Find customers who have ordered products from more than one category, showing their names and categories.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) AS category_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 1

natural_language: List all customers who have only cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) = COUNT(o.order_id);

natural_language: Find customers who signed up in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-12-31';

natural_language: Identify all products that have been sold in orders exceeding their average price, along with the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products)

natural_language: Show the total revenue generated from products in the 'furniture' category by each employee with region 'central'.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE e.region = 'central' AND p.category = 'furniture' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Get the total sales for each product by joining the order table and order items, only including products with more than $200 in sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 200

natural_language: Get the details of orders placed by customers in the 'vip' segment that are currently pending.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_date, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Find the customers who have purchased the most expensive product in the last three months, along with the purchase date.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE oi.unit_price = (SELECT MAX(price) FROM products) AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '3 month';

natural_language: List all VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Identify the overlapping cities where both retail and corporate customers are spending, showing the total spending for each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'retail' THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END) AS retail_spending, SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'corporate' THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END) AS corporate_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'retail' THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN c.segment = 'corporate' THEN o.total_amount ELSE 0 END) > 0

natural_language: List the total quantity and revenue for each product sold, only for products that have generated more than $500 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Get all employees with the full name 'John Smith'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name = 'John Smith';

natural_language: Show all customers along with their total order amounts, including those with no orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COALESCE(SUM(o.total_amount), 0) AS total_order_amount FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the customer information for all customers who have made a purchase of more than $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.total_amount > 500;

natural_language: Get the names of employees who have completed orders and their corresponding order IDs.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, orders.order_id FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the total number of employees in the company.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees;

natural_language: List the full names and email addresses of all customers who have completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders with a total amount under $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND total_amount < 50;

natural_language: Show the total sales for each product, filtering for products that have generated more than $1,000 in revenue from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of orders and total sales amount for each city.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: Get the order date and total amount for all orders made by customers in the city of Chicago.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_date, o.total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Chicago';

natural_language: List all customers along with their total order amounts from completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: List all employees and the number of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) as total_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find out which products have a sales total that surpasses 5000 and list them by total sales.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000 ORDER BY total_sales DESC

natural_language: Show the total number of orders and total revenue generated from each product category, filtering categories with revenue above $5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Identify the top 5 products based on the total revenue generated, and include the corresponding category and total quantity sold.
sql_query:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue
FROM products p
JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get a count of all customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Show the total revenue from products in the 'Electronics' category sold through completed orders, categorized by product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List all customers who signed up in 2020 and are from 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31' AND city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Find customers who have placed more than 5 orders, including the total amount spent and their segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.segment HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Identify the five employees with the best average order amount, including their names and average order amount.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY average_order_amount DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Identify the top 10 customers by total spent, including the total number of orders and their segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.segment ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 10

natural_language: Identify the categories with the highest total cost, but only include categories with total costs over $1500.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) > 1500

natural_language: Retrieve the signup dates and total order amounts of corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.signup_date, SUM(o.total_amount) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY c.signup_date;

natural_language: List all customers who have spent more than the average spending of their segment and provide their total spending amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_segment_spending) FROM (SELECT SUM(o2.total_amount) AS total_segment_spending FROM customers AS c2 JOIN orders AS o2 ON c2.customer_id = o2.customer_id GROUP BY c2.segment) AS avg_segment)

natural_language: Find the average order total for customers from the city 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: Get a list of orders with their total amounts sorted by customer name.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id ORDER BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get the highest total revenue generated by any product in the retail segment, considering only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders and their corresponding customers who live in 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York';

natural_language: List all unique cities where customers have placed orders, along with the total number of orders from each city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Find all employees who have completed orders and their respective regions.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT e.full_name, e.region FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List customers who signed up in December 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM signup_date) = 12 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2021;

natural_language: Get the total amount spent by each customer along with their email addresses.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.email, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id GROUP BY customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the cities of customers along with the total amount of their completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, SUM(o.total_amount) as total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Determine the total number of products sold and the total revenue generated from those products for orders in the pending status.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get the total number of distinct products ordered by customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS distinct_products_ordered FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Find the average price of products ordered by customers in the corporate segment and the total number of distinct products ordered.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS average_product_price, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS total_distinct_products FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate';

natural_language: Identify the products that generated more than $1000 in total sales, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Get the employees who have the highest commission rate and the number of completed orders they have processed, including their average total amount per order.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE e.commission_rate = (SELECT MAX(commission_rate) FROM employees) AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: List all segments and the total number of customers in each segment that have placed at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS total_customers FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Find the average price and total quantity sold of products in a specific category for orders placed by retail customers, organized by product name.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, AVG(p.price) AS average_price, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_name

natural_language: Get all completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the average commission rate for employees who processed orders above the average order total across all orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(e.commission_rate) as average_commission FROM employees e WHERE e.employee_id IN (SELECT o.employee_id FROM orders o WHERE o.total_amount > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders));

natural_language: Get all customers with 'John' in their full name.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE full_name LIKE '%John%';

natural_language: Find all products that have never been sold by any employee in the west region, along with their categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id LEFT JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region != 'west' OR e.employee_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Count the number of completed orders per customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) as completed_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Count the number of products supplied by each category that have been ordered at least once, including total quantity and unique product count.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS unique_products, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Find the maximum total order amount for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, MAX(o.total_amount) AS max_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List product categories along with their total sales amounts, but exclude those categories with total sales below $15,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 15000

natural_language: Find all customers signed up after June 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date > '2023-06-01';

natural_language: Find the average number of products ordered per order, segmented by the order status.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, AVG(item_count) AS avg_items_per_order FROM (SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS item_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id) AS order_summary JOIN orders o ON order_summary.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: Identify the employees who have sold more than 100 items in total, along with their commission rate.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.commission_rate HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: List all pending orders placed after January 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND order_date > '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Identify the customers who have ordered products from more than three different categories and show their full name along with the total amount spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Find all products in the 'electronics' category that have been ordered and the total number sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the list of customers who have made orders totaling more than the average order amount for their segment, including their total spent and number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_order_value) FROM (SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total_order_value FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment) AS avg_per_segment)

natural_language: Get the total sales per product category for completed orders that exceed $1,000 in total amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Get all employees located in the 'west' region with a commission rate of 15%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'west' AND commission_rate = 0.15;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales by product category, but only include categories with total sales greater than $5000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Get the full names of customers and their signup dates along with their order statuses.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.signup_date, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Calculate the total profit made from each product category in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM((oi.unit_price - p.cost) * oi.quantity) AS total_profit FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Retrieve the number of products sold and total revenue for each product in the 'electronics' category, excluding those with total sales less than 1000.
