sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 1000

natural_language: Identify the regions with the highest average order amount for corporate customers, filtering out any region with an average below 300.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY e.region HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) >= 300

natural_language: Find out which products have been ordered and their corresponding total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: List the names of employees and the count of orders they have processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: List all completed orders along with customer names and their respective order dates.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_date FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List the total number of unique products ordered and the total revenue per category, excluding categories with less than $2,000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS unique_products, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) >= 2000

natural_language: Determine the ratio of completed to cancelled orders for each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_orders, (SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0)) AS completion_ratio FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List the customer segments and the corresponding orders placed in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Show all products that are categorized as 'Clothing'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Clothing';

natural_language: Find the employees who have handled the most orders and their corresponding total sales amount, limited to the top 5.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_handled, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name ORDER BY orders_handled DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Find the top 5 products by total sales amount and include the number of units sold for each.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List all employees along with the number of orders they processed and the total sales amount, excluding employees with no processed orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 0

natural_language: List the products that have been sold the most along with their total earnings, excluding those that haven’t sold at all.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_earnings FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 0 ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC

natural_language: Retrieve the signup dates of customers who made purchases in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Retrieve the highest priced product in each category with the total sales amount per category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, MAX(p.price) AS highest_price, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Retrieve a list of all customers who have purchased products from multiple categories, including their total expenditure.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_expenditure FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 1

natural_language: Get all products that have been ordered by customers in the retail segment and find the total number of orders and total quantity sold for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the average price of products sold in each city, but only include those cities where the average price exceeds $50.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, AVG(p.price) AS average_price FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.city HAVING AVG(p.price) > 50

natural_language: Calculate the total expenditure of each customer segment on products in a specific category, and include the category name.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_expenditure FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment, p.category

natural_language: Determine the most popular product category among corporate customers based on the total quantity sold and group the results by category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC;

natural_language: Calculate the total cost of products sold for each employee in the west region, showing employee name and total cost.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE e.region = 'west' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Find the number of products sold by category for orders placed in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 month' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Calculate the profit for each employee by subtracting the total cost of sold products from their total sales for orders from VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) - SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS profit FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY e.full_name

natural_language: Find the total amount of all completed orders handled by employees in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(orders.total_amount) FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' AND employees.region = 'east';

natural_language: Retrieve all products that are available (price greater than cost).
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > cost;

natural_language: Get a list of customers and their corresponding orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_id FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the customers who have placed the highest number of orders but have the lowest total spending, and return their names and order counts.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY total_orders DESC, total_spending ASC LIMIT 10;

natural_language: Find the average order size in terms of total amount for each customer segment along with the total number of orders for every segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) as avg_order_size, COUNT(o.order_id) as total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get a list of products that have been ordered by corporate customers, along with the total quantity sold and total revenue generated, filtering for products with total revenue greater than $1000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Retrieve the employee names and their commission rates for orders exceeding $1000.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.total_amount > 1000;

natural_language: Identify which products have been sold the most and their total sales amount.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC;

natural_language: Retrieve the products sold in the last month along with the total quantity sold for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30 day' GROUP BY p.product_id;

natural_language: Get the total number of completed orders made by customers from 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Los Angeles' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the signup date of customers along with the total amount of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.signup_date, SUM(orders.total_amount) as total_spent FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the total income generated by each product category from orders that are pending, including only those categories with more than $1000 in total income.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_income FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who registered in the month of January.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and total revenue generated from each product category, while excluding categories that generated less than $5,000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000

natural_language: Calculate the total amount of completed orders for each product category where the total exceeds $30,000, showing category names and total amounts.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_amount FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 30000

natural_language: Calculate the total number of products sold and their total revenue per category for those categories with more than 500 units sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Show all completed orders made by customer ID 10.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 10 AND status = 'completed';

natural_language: Show all completed orders made in February 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 2 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: Count the number of customers that signed up in 2023.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2023;

natural_language: Show all employees with less than 5 years of experience.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE employee_id < 5;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders made by a specific employee with ID 3.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE employee_id = 3 AND status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get customers with their signup date and the total number of orders they have made.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, customers.signup_date, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.full_name, customers.signup_date;

natural_language: Calculate the total number of items sold and the total revenue from completed orders for corporate customers, differentiated by the product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: List the product categories and the total quantity sold for each category, but only include categories that have sold more than 100 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Retrieve the total quantity of products sold per category, only including categories where total quantity sold exceeds 100.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: List all products with names that contain the word 'Gadget'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%Gadget%';

natural_language: Find the latest order date for each customer along with their name and total number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, MAX(o.order_date) AS latest_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Count the number of unique customers for each product and calculate their total purchase amounts, focusing on those products that generated more than $3000 in revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS unique_customers, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 3000

natural_language: Get the average order total for each customer's segment.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, AVG(orders.total_amount) AS average_order FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Show all products that are above their cost price by more than $20.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > cost + 20;

natural_language: List the top 5 products based on total sales, including the number of orders each product has been sold in.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_quantity, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) as order_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get the total number of orders placed by each customer.
sql_query: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id;

natural_language: List the average order amount per customer and filter it to show only those who have spent over $1000.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING AVG(o.total_amount) > 1000

natural_language: Find the employees from the east region who have processed cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled' AND employees.region = 'east';

natural_language: Calculate the total profit for each product sold in completed orders, where profit is defined as (price - cost) * quantity.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM((p.price - p.cost) * oi.quantity) AS total_profit FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List all orders along with the customer full name for customers in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: List total sales amount by product for all products that have been ordered in a cancelled status.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS sales_amount FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List all products that cost more than $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost > 30.00;

natural_language: Find the number of different products ordered by each customer and the total spent, filtering out customers with fewer than 2 unique products.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) >= 2

natural_language: Identify the customers who have ordered products from every category at least once, along with their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spending FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT category) FROM products)

natural_language: Get all customers who have placed a cancelled order.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: List the products that have generated the highest total revenue, along with the total quantity sold, only considering orders completed in the last year.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 year' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales amount for each product category sold by employees from the 'west' region, along with the number of orders that were completed, grouped by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Show all order items for a specific order ID.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 456;

natural_language: Fetch the list of all completed orders along with customer names and order dates.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Identify all customers who live in 'New York' and have made at least 3 purchases from the 'Electronics' category, including their total spending.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.city = 'New York' AND p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3

natural_language: Calculate the total cost of products sold per category, and show categories where the total cost is greater than $10,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) > 10000

natural_language: Find the product categories and their total quantities sold only for orders that are still pending.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get all orders that were cancelled before July 1, 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'cancelled' AND order_date < '2023-07-01';

natural_language: List all products in the fashion category that cost more than $25.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'fashion' AND cost > 25;

natural_language: Determine the number of employees that have processed orders in each region, and also calculate the average commission rate for those employees.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, COUNT(DISTINCT e.employee_id) AS employee_count, AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission_rate FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region;

natural_language: Find the details of customers who live in 'central' and have made a 'completed' order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'central' AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the total number of orders placed by each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: List all orders with an order date in September 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2023-09-01' AND '2023-09-30';

natural_language: Find the customer who spent the highest amount on a single order, including their full name and the order amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(o.total_amount) AS highest_order_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY highest_order_amount DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get a list of employees with their total commission earned from orders, only including those who have processed more than 10 orders and categorize by region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, e.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.region, e.full_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 10

natural_language: List the names of customers who have signed up after January 1, 2022, along with their order counts.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers LEFT JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.signup_date > '2022-01-01' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who signed up in December 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2022-12-01' AND '2022-12-31';

natural_language: Retrieve the highest priced product sold in each category along with the total quantity sold and the corresponding employee who sold it.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, MAX(p.price) AS highest_price, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, e.full_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY p.category, e.full_name;

natural_language: List products along with the total quantity sold for each category, only including categories with total quantity sold greater than 50.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: List the top 5 products by total revenue generated and also show how many times they were sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS times_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: List customers who have made orders in the last month along with their total ordered amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Get a list of all customers who have never placed an order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;

natural_language: Get the average number of items per order for each customer segment, only considering segments with at least 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(total_items) AS avg_items_per_order FROM (SELECT oi.order_id, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS total_items FROM order_items AS oi GROUP BY oi.order_id) AS items JOIN orders AS o ON items.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 10

natural_language: Count the number of orders for each product sold in the retail segment, only considering orders that are completed.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS orders_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: List all customers with their corresponding orders where the order status is completed.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_id, orders.order_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List products that have been sold at a total revenue of more than $5000 and have a price above $100.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 5000 AND p.price > 100

natural_language: List all orders where the total amount is greater than or equal to $500.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount >= 500;

natural_language: Get the email addresses of customers who live in 'New York' and have cancelled their orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'New York' AND o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Identify the top 5 products by sales amount, including the corresponding product category and the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated from products belonging to the category 'Electronics' for orders made by corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND p.category = 'Electronics';

natural_language: Fetch the full names of employees who have handled cancelled orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT e.full_name FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Get the customers along with the most expensive product they've purchased, including the product price.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, MAX(p.price) AS most_expensive_product_price FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id

natural_language: Find the total number of pending orders for each employee in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS pending_orders FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending' AND employees.region = 'east' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: List all products in the 'furniture' category that have been sold by employees in the 'west' region, including the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE p.category = 'furniture' AND e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Retrieve all products priced exactly at 50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price = 50;

natural_language: Show the full name and city of corporate customers with pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Find the total amounts of completed orders along with the names of customers who made them.
sql_query: SELECT o.total_amount, c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the average price of products sold in each category, only including categories with total product sales exceeding $10000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.price) AS avg_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 10000

natural_language: Retrieve the average commission rate for employees who have sold more than 10 different products, categorized by their region.
sql_query: SELECT e.region, AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN (SELECT o.employee_id, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS product_count FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.employee_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) > 10) AS emp_sales ON e.employee_id = emp_sales.employee_id GROUP BY e.region

natural_language: Get the list of customers who have placed pending orders and their order dates.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_date FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Identify the products that have been sold more than 10 times in completed orders, and list the customer segments of those who bought them.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, c.segment FROM products p INNER JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name, c.segment HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10;

natural_language: List all products that were ordered by customers in the 'corporate' segment, along with the total quantity sold for each product, and the total revenue generated from those products.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name

natural_language: Find all orders that have a total amount less than $50.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount < 50;

natural_language: Retrieve all products that have a cost less than or equal to $30.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE cost <= 30;

natural_language: Show all customers who live in Seattle and were signed up before 2019.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Seattle' AND signup_date < '2019-01-01';

natural_language: Retrieve all customers who live in 'San Francisco' or 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city IN ('San Francisco', 'Los Angeles');

natural_language: Get a list of employees along with their commission rate and the total amount of orders they processed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.commission_rate, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_value FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id;

natural_language: Retrieve each employee's total sales, as well as their commission earned from those sales, for sales over $1,000.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * e.commission_rate) AS total_commission FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000

natural_language: Get the list of all completed orders made in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Get the total profit for each product category, calculating profit as total sales minus total cost.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) - SUM(p.cost * oi.quantity) AS total_profit FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the list of products along with their total sales and quantities sold, showing only those that sold less than 20 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) < 20

natural_language: Find all employees in the east region with a commission rate of 15%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE region = 'east' AND commission_rate = 0.15;

natural_language: List the cities and count of customers from each city who have completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, COUNT(customers.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.city;

natural_language: List the unique cities of customers who have placed orders in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Find the top 5 customers with the highest total spending, including their full name and email, ordered by total amount spent.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.email ORDER BY total_spent DESC OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 5 ROWS ONLY

natural_language: Find the average price of products ordered in the 'electronics' category.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(products.price) AS average_price FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id WHERE products.category = 'electronics';

natural_language: Count the number of customers in the VIP segment.
sql_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS vip_customers_count FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Find the total revenue generated by completed orders categorized by customer segments.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the average number of items per order for each category, but only include categories where the average items exceed 4.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_items_per_order FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(oi.quantity) > 4

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders made in the year 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date >= '2023-01-01';

natural_language: Identify employees who have the highest average sales per order, and indicate the segment of customers they serve the most.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_sales_per_order FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY e.full_name, c.segment ORDER BY average_sales_per_order DESC

natural_language: Calculate the total sales by product category for orders placed by VIP customers.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) as total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Get the product categories with their total sales and the average selling price, only include categories with sales greater than $15,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS average_price FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 15000

natural_language: Get the total sales and number of orders for each product category for products where the total sales are more than $2,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: Get the total number of items sold for each product along with their category, ordered by the total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, p.category ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC;

natural_language: Find the segment of customers who have placed completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get a list of customers who have placed more than 3 orders, along with their total spent amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 3

natural_language: Find the most popular product in terms of the number of units sold and how many distinct customers purchased it.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units_sold, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Retrieve the count of orders placed per segment for each city, only including those cities with more than 10 customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city, c.segment HAVING COUNT(c.customer_id) > 10

natural_language: Determine the total revenue for each product category derived from orders placed by customers from 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Los Angeles' GROUP BY p.category

natural_language: Retrieve all corporate customers from Miami.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate' AND city = 'Miami';

natural_language: Find all orders with a total amount of exactly $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE total_amount = 200;

natural_language: Get a breakdown of total sales by product category for orders made by retail customers only in the last six months.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.segment = 'retail' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 month' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List all products in the grocery category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'grocery';

natural_language: Show the signup date and email of customers who have placed pending orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.signup_date, c.email FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Get the product names and costs of products in the 'furniture' category.
sql_query: SELECT product_name, cost FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture';

natural_language: Get all retail customers who signed up in 2022.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail' AND signup_date >= '2022-01-01' AND signup_date < '2023-01-01';

natural_language: List all customers and their order counts, but include only those customers who have spent more than the average customer spend across all orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_spent) FROM (SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total_spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) AS avg_spend)

natural_language: List the average total order amounts per segment and the percentage of orders that are completed in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(o.total_amount) AS average_order_amount, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(o.order_id) AS completion_rate FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amounts for orders made by customers in a specific city, grouping by status.
sql_query: SELECT o.status, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.city = 'Los Angeles' GROUP BY o.status;

natural_language: List the customer email, order status, and total amount for all orders made by retail customers.
sql_query: SELECT customers.email, orders.status, orders.total_amount FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Find all orders associated with a specific employee.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE employee_id = 1;

natural_language: Show the names of customers who have not ordered any products from the 'fashion' category and how many orders they have.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category != 'fashion' OR p.category IS NULL GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: List the total revenue by product for products having a total order count of more than 10, including only completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(oi.order_id) > 10

natural_language: Get the total number of orders made by each customer.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the most profitable product in terms of profit margin sold by each employee in the last six months.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, p.product_name, MAX((oi.unit_price - p.cost) * oi.quantity) AS max_profit FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '6 month' GROUP BY e.full_name, p.product_name;

natural_language: Find the total number of orders by segment (retail, corporate, vip).
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders made by customers in the city of New York.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE city = 'New York');

natural_language: Find all products in the 'furniture' category with a price less than $200.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'furniture' AND price < 200;

natural_language: Retrieve the cities of customers along with the total amount of their respective completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.city, SUM(orders.total_amount) as completed_orders_total FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the average quantity of products sold per order for each segment, only including segments with more than 10 orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 10

natural_language: Determine the total costs incurred by customers in each city for completed orders, grouped by customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.segment, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city, c.segment;

natural_language: Find the names of customers who live in the city 'New York' and the orders they have placed.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_id FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'New York';

natural_language: List employees who have sold more than 100 products in the last year.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2022-10-01' GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: List the order details along with the names of the customers who placed them.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name, o.order_date FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

natural_language: Get a list of customers who have made more than 5 orders, including their total spend and their signup date.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, c.signup_date FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: Count the number of orders with at least one order item for each product category where total order count is above 5.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) > 5

natural_language: List all order items for a specific order id.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id = 12345;

natural_language: List orders that have more than 2 products, including the customer's full name and the total order amount.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.order_id, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.full_name, o.order_id HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 2;

natural_language: Show the total commission earned by employees based on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount * employees.commission_rate) as total_commission FROM orders JOIN employees ON orders.employee_id = employees.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.employee_id;

natural_language: Calculate the total spending on products from the 'Furniture' category for each customer, only including those customers who have made at least 3 orders and have spent more than $700.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Furniture' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) >= 3 AND SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 700

natural_language: Find the average quantity of products sold per completed order for corporate customers.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Find the employee names who have processed orders that include products from the 'Electronics' category, along with the total number of such orders.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Electronics' GROUP BY e.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the total amount of completed orders and their respective employee names.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_completed FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: List all completed orders from a specific employee identified by employee_id = 2.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE employee_id = 2 AND status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find the total number of orders and total sales for each employee, along with their region.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, e.region, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e LEFT JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.full_name, e.region;

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders placed by customers in the 'vip' segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE segment = 'vip');

natural_language: Find the average cost of products sold in completed orders, categorized by product category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(p.cost) AS average_cost FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: List all products in the 'Furniture' category with a price less than $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture' AND price < 100;

natural_language: Retrieve all customers from Chicago in the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE city = 'Chicago' AND segment = 'retail';

natural_language: List all completed orders placed in March 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date BETWEEN '2023-03-01' AND '2023-03-31';

natural_language: Retrieve the names of employees who have completed orders totaling more than $500.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT e.full_name FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.total_amount > 500 AND o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Identify customers who have a higher than average total spending, grouped by city, while also counting how many orders they made.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total_amount) FROM orders)

natural_language: List all products that have the name containing 'phone'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%phone%';

natural_language: List the product names and prices of products that cost more than $100.
sql_query: SELECT product_name, price FROM products WHERE cost > 100;

natural_language: Get all completed orders made on '2023-05-15'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date = '2023-05-15' AND status = 'completed';

natural_language: Compile a list of products that have been ordered by 'corporate' customers more than the average count of orders per customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'corporate' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) AS sub);

natural_language: List the top 3 products by total sales amount, including the product name and total amount sold.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Get a list of products and the number of times they have been ordered, along with the corresponding order IDs.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, order_items.quantity, order_items.order_id FROM order_items JOIN products ON order_items.product_id = products.product_id;

natural_language: Retrieve all orders placed by customer with ID 5.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 5;

natural_language: Find all products that have been sold more than 10 times and show their total revenue, but only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING COUNT(oi.order_item_id) > 10

natural_language: List all employees with a name that starts with 'A'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE full_name LIKE 'A%';

natural_language: Get the total amount of all completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total_completed_orders FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the total quantity sold for products in the 'electronics' category, showing only those sales linked to completed orders by employees from the 'west' region.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' AND o.status = 'completed' AND e.region = 'west' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: What is the total value of orders and the number of items sold for each product name, including only those sold in 'completed' orders?
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_order_value, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_items_sold FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name;

natural_language: Get all products that belong to the 'electronics' category and cost less than 300.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'electronics' AND price < 300;

natural_language: Identify the customers who have placed the largest number of orders along with their total spending and their most frequent product category.
sql_query: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, (SELECT p.category FROM products p INNER JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id INNER JOIN orders o2 ON oi.order_id = o2.order_id WHERE o2.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY COUNT(oi.order_item_id) DESC LIMIT 1) AS most_frequent_category FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id;

natural_language: List all employees and their commission rates for orders that have been cancelled.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT employees.full_name, employees.commission_rate FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Find the total number of completed orders for each customer.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: Show the total number of orders made by each customer segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) as total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Get all orders that were placed in the last week.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7 day';

natural_language: Identify the highest spending customer in the east region and retrieve their full name and total spent amount, focusing on completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE e.region = 'east' AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.full_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: List customers and their corresponding signup dates who have made at least one completed order.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.signup_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Retrieve the product categories that have an average revenue from completed orders exceeding $2000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS average_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2000

natural_language: Find the total number of products sold by each employee for orders that are pending, but only include employees who have sold more than 100 items in total.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_products_sold FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY e.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 100

natural_language: Find the customers who have spent the most on 'electronics' products, along with their total expenditure and the number of orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_spent, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

natural_language: Identify products and their total sales for the last year, but only for those products with total sales over $15,000.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 YEAR' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 15000

natural_language: List all employees along with the orders they have completed.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, o.order_id FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Find all employees working under a specific employee ID.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE employee_id = 3;

natural_language: Find the highest order total for each segment of customers and how many orders were made in each segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, MAX(o.total_amount) AS highest_order_total, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: Identify the top 5 products by total sales amount, including their categories.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get the product with the highest total sales amount along with the category it belongs to and the number of distinct customers who purchased it.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id ORDER BY SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Get the total sales and average quantity sold for each product in the 'furniture' category, but only include products that have sold more than 50 units in total.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, AVG(oi.quantity) AS avg_quantity_sold FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'furniture' GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 50

natural_language: Get all products that have 'new' in their name.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%new%';

natural_language: List all orders with their respective customer's full name and the city they reside in.
sql_query: SELECT o.order_id, c.full_name, c.city FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the average price of products sold in the 'clothing' category by orders with 'pending' status.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(p.price) AS avg_price FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE p.category = 'clothing' AND o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: List the customers who have spent above average in their segment and their order count.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.total_amount) > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM (SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total FROM orders AS o2 JOIN customers AS c2 ON o2.customer_id = c2.customer_id GROUP BY c2.segment) AS segment_totals)

natural_language: Get the list of customers and the status of their most recent order.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.status FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_date = (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM orders WHERE customer_id = c.customer_id);

natural_language: Retrieve the full names and emails of all customers from the city 'New York'.
sql_query: SELECT full_name, email FROM customers WHERE city = 'New York';

natural_language: Get customer names along with the total amount of their orders and their segments.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_amount, c.segment FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.full_name, c.segment;

natural_language: Retrieve the top 3 employees with the highest average order total, along with their region and average order total.
sql_query: SELECT e.employee_id, e.full_name, e.region, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_total FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY avg_order_total DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: Identify which product category generated the most revenue from orders placed by customers in the city of New York.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE c.city = 'New York' GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

natural_language: Select the full names of customers who signed up in 2022.
sql_query: SELECT full_name FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-12-31';

natural_language: Retrieve customers and their order totals for orders placed in 2022.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) as order_total FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM orders.order_date) = 2022 GROUP BY customers.full_name;

natural_language: List customers who are in the VIP segment along with the order ID and status of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.full_name, orders.order_id, orders.status FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'vip';

natural_language: Get all customers who are part of the retail segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail';

natural_language: List the customer segments and the count of their completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT customers.segment, COUNT(orders.order_id) AS completed_order_count FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' GROUP BY customers.segment;

natural_language: Find the names of customers and the total amounts of their orders that are pending.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, o.total_amount FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending';

natural_language: Find the number of unique products sold by each customer segment, filtering for segments that sold more than 10 unique products.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) AS unique_products_sold FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.product_id) > 10

natural_language: List all customers who signed up in the year 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM signup_date) = 2021;

natural_language: List the employees who have processed more than 20 orders and their average commission rate, sorted by average commission rate descending.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission_rate FROM employees AS e JOIN orders AS o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 20 ORDER BY average_commission_rate DESC

natural_language: Get the total commission rate of all employees.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(commission_rate) FROM employees;

natural_language: Retrieve the total number of unique products ordered and the total revenue generated from completed orders, segmented by customer city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.product_id) AS unique_products_ordered, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.city;

natural_language: Get the commission rates for all employees located in the east region.
sql_query: SELECT commission_rate FROM employees WHERE region = 'east';

natural_language: Get the total number of products sold and total revenue generated for each product, filtering only those that sold more than 10 units.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_sold, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity) > 10

natural_language: Retrieve products with name containing 'gadget'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE product_name LIKE '%gadget%';

natural_language: Find the order dates and statuses of orders that were placed by retail customers.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_date, orders.status FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.segment = 'retail';

natural_language: Find the cities where customers who have placed cancelled orders reside.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Count the number of products in each category sold in completed orders, but only include categories where the sale count exceeds 15.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, COUNT(oi.product_id) AS product_count FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(oi.product_id) > 15

natural_language: List the order date and total amount for orders placed by customers from 'Los Angeles'.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_date, orders.total_amount FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'Los Angeles';

natural_language: Retrieve all completed orders placed in 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' AND order_date BETWEEN '2021-01-01' AND '2021-12-31';

natural_language: Get the total number of orders and total revenue generated by each employee, ordering by revenue.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY e.employee_id ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

natural_language: Find all orders where the order date is in January 2023.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 1 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023;

natural_language: List all customers and their total spending, only for orders that are pending.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'pending' GROUP BY c.full_name;

natural_language: Retrieve the employee names and their total sales for all orders processed in the central region.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE employees.region = 'central' GROUP BY employees.full_name;

natural_language: Find all products in the 'Electronics' category.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Electronics';

natural_language: Find the average commission rate for employees who processed completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT AVG(e.commission_rate) AS average_commission FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: List all pending orders with a total amount greater than $100.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND total_amount > 100;

natural_language: Count distinct customers who have made orders for products in more than three categories, and find out which segments they belong to.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS distinct_customers FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY c.segment HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) > 3

natural_language: Retrieve the distinct cities where customers have placed at least one completed order.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'completed';

natural_language: Get the count of orders for each customer segment, including the total revenue generated from those orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) as total_revenue FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment;

natural_language: List all products that have been ordered by VIP customers, including the total quantity ordered and the total sales amount for each product.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' GROUP BY p.product_name

natural_language: List the average price of products sold in each category for completed orders, but only for those categories where the average price is above $50.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, AVG(oi.unit_price) AS avg_price FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING AVG(oi.unit_price) > 50

natural_language: Retrieve the average order amount for customers in the VIP segment who have made more than 3 orders, grouped by city.
sql_query: SELECT c.city, AVG(o.total_amount) AS avg_order_amount FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.segment = 'vip' AND c.customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) > 3) GROUP BY c.city

natural_language: List the most profitable product categories based on the difference between total sales and total costs.
