sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS profit FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) > 0 ORDER BY profit DESC

natural_language: Find all customers who have made purchases exclusively from the 'electronics' category and provide the total amount they spent along with their segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category = 'electronics' GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = 1

natural_language: Show all customers who registered in December 2021.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE signup_date BETWEEN '2021-12-01' AND '2021-12-31';

natural_language: Show customers who are in the retail segment and reside in Chicago.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE segment = 'retail' AND city = 'Chicago';

natural_language: Get a list of products and the corresponding total amount of orders they were part of.
sql_query: SELECT products.product_name, SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products JOIN order_items ON products.product_id = order_items.product_id GROUP BY products.product_name;

natural_language: List the top 3 products by total quantity sold in completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) as total_quantity FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 3;

natural_language: List all cancelled orders along with their total amounts and the customers who made them.
sql_query: SELECT orders.order_id, orders.total_amount, customers.full_name FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE orders.status = 'cancelled';

natural_language: Show the top 3 categories by total sales amount for completed orders, but only include categories where total sales exceed $10000.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 10000 ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 3

natural_language: List the top 5 customers by total amount spent, including their email and their primary order date.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.email, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent, MIN(o.order_date) AS first_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Get the full names and cities of customers who have made at least one order.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT c.full_name, c.city FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

natural_language: Retrieve the total costs of products sold in completed orders for each category.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * p.cost) AS total_cost FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Retrieve the top 5 customers who spent the most, along with the employee who managed their orders and the count of their orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, e.full_name AS employee_name, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_spent FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id GROUP BY c.full_name, e.full_name ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5;

natural_language: Identify the highest selling product for each employee, including the employee's name, product name, and total quantity sold.
sql_query: SELECT e.full_name AS employee_name, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY e.employee_id, p.product_id ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC;

natural_language: Retrieve all employees with a commission rate greater than 15%.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE commission_rate > 0.15;

natural_language: List customer names with their order count who have made purchases in both the 'Clothing' and 'Electronics' categories, but only for completed orders.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND p.category IN ('Clothing', 'Electronics') GROUP BY c.full_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = 2

natural_language: Get the total number of completed and cancelled orders along with their respective average total amounts for customers segmented by retail and corporate.
sql_query: SELECT c.segment, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_orders, AVG(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN o.total_amount END) AS average_completed_order, COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 END) AS cancelled_orders, AVG(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN o.total_amount END) AS average_cancelled_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.segment

natural_language: Identify which employees have an above-average sales performance in completed orders, based on total sales compared to their peers.
sql_query: WITH EmployeeSales AS (SELECT e.employee_id, SUM(o.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM employees e JOIN orders o ON e.employee_id = o.employee_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.employee_id), AverageSales AS (SELECT AVG(total_sales) AS avg_sales FROM EmployeeSales) SELECT e.full_name FROM EmployeeSales es JOIN employees e ON es.employee_id = e.employee_id WHERE es.total_sales > (SELECT avg_sales FROM AverageSales)

natural_language: List all customers with their email addresses who have made orders.
sql_query: SELECT DISTINCT customers.full_name, customers.email FROM customers JOIN orders ON customers.customer_id = orders.customer_id;

natural_language: Find the customer with the most orders and the total number of their orders, including their segment.
sql_query: SELECT c.full_name, c.segment, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name, c.segment ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1

natural_language: Get the total revenue generated from all orders placed by customers from 'Chicago'.
sql_query: SELECT SUM(orders.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id WHERE customers.city = 'Chicago';

natural_language: Retrieve the names and regions of employees who have processed completed orders in the last month.
sql_query: SELECT employees.full_name, employees.region FROM employees JOIN orders ON employees.employee_id = orders.employee_id WHERE orders.status = 'completed' AND orders.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '1 month';

natural_language: Identify how many orders have been placed for each product and their respective total revenue generated, filtering for products with revenue over $500.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, COUNT(oi.order_item_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_revenue FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name HAVING SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) > 500

natural_language: Retrieve a report of products sold by each employee, showing the employee's name, the product name, and the total quantity sold of each product.

natural_language: Find all orders placed on '2023-05-01'.

natural_language: Find all products whose total sales exceed $5000, along with the number of orders they have been part of.

natural_language: Get the total number of unique products sold by each employee, but only include employees with more than 20 completed orders.

natural_language: Summarize the total amount of sales for each product category and determine how each category contributes to overall revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS total_sales, (SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) / (SELECT SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) FROM order_items oi)) * 100 AS revenue_contribution FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.category;

natural_language: Retrieve the total sales amount for each product category sold by employees in the east region, showing the product category and the total sales amount for each category.
sql_query:
SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id

sql_query: SELECT total_amount FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed';

natural_language: List the top 5 products based on total quantity sold, only including products that made over $1000 in sales revenue.
sql_query: SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM products AS p JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 1000 ORDER BY total_quantity DESC LIMIT 5

natural_language: Find all order items for orders that have a status of 'pending'.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM order_items WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending');

natural_language: Find all orders made by customers in the 'corporate' segment.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM customers WHERE segment = 'corporate');

natural_language: Get products that belong to the 'Furniture' category and are priced below $300.
sql_query: SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = 'Furniture' AND price < 300;
